brief: Pixel 2 in fastboot, read only: unlocked, A/B both slots successful, stock A/B layout, old bootloader with no fastbootd; which Android sits on it is not known yet
question: What does the Pixel 2's bootloader say about the phone, and does Android still sit on it, judged from read-only variables only?
found:
Measured with `fastboot getvar all` (nothing flashed, booted or set): product walleye, hw-revision MP1, boot-mode FASTBOOT, unlocked yes, secure yes, kernel uefi, bootloader mw8998-003.0085.00, baseband g8998-00034-2006052136, slot-count 2, current-slot a, both slots successful=yes unbootable=no retry-count 0, max-download-size 512 MiB, avb 1.0.0 with user-settable key set, battery 4344 mV. Partitions listed with a size: boot_a/b 32 MiB raw, system_a/b 2560 MiB ext4, vendor_a/b 500 MiB ext4, userdata about 53 GiB ext4. is-userspace, slot-suffixes, snapshot-update-status and the sizes of vbmeta, dtbo and modem are not offered: an old bootloader, no fastbootd.
Inference: both slots carry the flags Android's boot control leaves after a good boot, and the partition table is the stock A/B layout, so an Android has run on each slot; userdata of 53 GiB fits the 64 GB model. Which Android, whether it still boots and whether userdata holds data is not known yet - the bootloader cannot say.
Not known yet: whether `fastboot boot` accepts a kernel built by us, and what it does afterwards; every Android reference measurement (sleep current, audio levels, sensors, boot time), backlog google-walleye-lab/android-reference-walleye - it needs the author to boot slot a, enable USB debugging and say when the phone is at the home screen; the paragraph is in the material README.
Next: a first `fastboot boot` try needs a kernel from the research sessions and devlab's fastboot mode (backlog lab-tools/devlab-fastboot-mode). The IMEI the bootloader prints was left out of the kept output.

brief: Android on the Pixel 2, read only: LineageOS 15 on stock vendor, 37 sensors, 12 s to system ready; sleep current and audio levels not known yet
question: What does Android do on the Pixel 2 as the author left it - build, sensors, battery, boot time, audio - measured read-only, with nothing installed or changed?
found:
Measured with plain adb reads, then back to fastboot with the slot flags unchanged: LineageOS 15 (Android 15, userdebug, built 2025-12-05, patch 2025-11-01) on a stock Android 11 Pixel 2 vendor image, kernel 4.4.302, MSM8998 (8 cores), 3.7 GB RAM, 51 GB data, 1080x1920. Sensorservice lists 37 sensors (LSM6DSM, AK09915, TMx490x, BMP280, AK8789, Elmyra, camera sync). Battery learned 2709 mAh of 2805 mAh design (96.6 %), 922 cycles. Boot, from the phone's own event log: system server at 8.3 s, package manager ready 10.1 s, ams_ready 12.0 s, boot animation done 17.8 s (kernel start to there; the bootloader stage is not counted). Audio config: stereo speaker output at 48 kHz.
Not known yet: sleep current (the phone was charging on USB, Wi-Fi was on, no meter; batterystats' long-run counters contradict themselves so no figure is given), audio levels (no tone source, no microphone), boot time from power-on, thermal limits, the real partition table. Needs next: a USB power meter or the battery path to measure standby with radios as stated, and a tone source plus a lab microphone.
Lesson for the keeper: adb authorization on this phone was lost at reboot until the author tapped Allow again, and the lab's adb server had to be restarted to see it; no reboot should be planned before "Always allow" is confirmed.

brief: Control (LineageOS walleye boot.img) and our e, f all refused with Load Error on slot b: the cause is the phone's state, not our image
question: Does a real stock-format walleye image boot by fastboot boot where ours is refused?
found: No. The LineageOS 22.2 boot.img, boot-e and boot-f each got Load Error ('Failed to load/authenticate boot image') within a second of the transfer; the phone stayed in fastboot (18d1:4ee0 in all 90 polls each); slot flags unchanged. Files: research/walleye-first-fastboot-boot/2026-11-17-control-e-f. So our images are not the (only) cause; open: dtbo/vbmeta/slot a flags, all writes or the author's.

brief: Best-known bootstrap: feedback channel first, vendor kernel as known-good, then mainline by fastboot boot; lk2nd is not for MSM8998/ABL; walleye skipped the vendor-kernel step
question: What is the best-known way to bootstrap an Android phone to mainline almost from zero (pmOS, Mobian/Halium, sdm845/sm8150 communities, MSM8998 siblings), and how does the walleye lane's work compare?
found:
THE METHOD, in order (pmOS Porting/Mainlining guides, Qualcomm mainline porting, Halium early-init, MSM8998 pages): 1 unlock, keep the stock boot.img and a way back to Android; read offsets/ids from it. 2 Get a feedback channel BEFORE mainline: UART first, then simple-framebuffer, ramoops last (pmOS order); for a no-display phone the USB gadget shell is the channel. 3 Vendor kernel first as a known-good: Halium/UBports/Droidian boot the vendor kernel with their own initramfs (telnet 192.168.2.15, break= levels) - it proves image format, offsets, cmdline, gadget, and shows ids, rails, reserved memory. pmOS recommends a downstream port as the base but no MSM8998 sibling did it; they went straight to mainline. 4 Board dts from msm8998-mtp: fix model/compatible/board-id, delete CoreSight nodes, match regulators, clk_ignore_unused (still the normal first flag, Dybcio 2025). 5 Image.gz + dtb appended, mkbootimg base 0 page 4096, initramfs with debug-shell and USB gadget; fastboot boot (OnePlus 5, Mi 6, Pixel 3 XL with a stub dtbo; OnePlus 5T OxygenOS 9 cannot fastboot boot - flash instead). 6 First shell over USB peripheral (QMP + QUSB2 PHY, dr_mode peripheral); Pixel 2 XL reached exactly this, black screen. 7 Then UFS (not on Sony), display, touch, radios; upstream with b4.
LK2ND: not a route. Its device list stops at msm8996, msm8998 is '?' in targets.md, no Pixel, and it is an LK fork loaded by LK-based aboot; Pixel 2 runs a Qualcomm ABL/UEFI-derived bootloader. Pixel 3/sdm845 recipe is plain fastboot boot plus a stub dtbo, not lk2nd. U-Boot as second stage under ABL exists for sdm845 (FOSDEM 2024), not known for msm8998. Whether an LK image could run under ABL is not known yet.
WALLEYE LANE vs THE METHOD: done - stock ids and header read from the public LineageOS image, boot images a-f (17 checks), gadget initramfs proven in QEMU, minimal dts, control test, and the finding that Load Error follows the slot's successful flag (control accepted only from the first state). Gaps: (a) step 3 never done - no image has run a kernel on this phone, so cmdline, ids, rails, ramoops address, and the gadget on real hardware are unseen; (b) step 2 - no feedback channel chosen: UART needs a cable and an oem decision, ramoops address unverified, simplefb unlikely (command-mode DSC panel); (c) the order: the lane went to its own mainline image before any known-good boot. The control (LineageOS boot.img, vendor 4.4 kernel) is accepted from the first state but then left USB with no sign for 6+ min, so even a stock image gives no feedback on this phone yet.
NOT KNOWN YET: whether the vendor kernel in the control reaches a configfs gadget (LineageOS kernels normally do for adb); whether fastboot oem uart enable persists; walleye's dtbo overlay id; first-shell method on taimen (flash vs fastboot boot); sm8150 practice and the FOSDEM 2024 slides were not read. pmOS wiki now at wiki.nura.eco behind a bot wall; read as raw wikitext.

brief: First fastboot boot tries on the Pixel 2: try a stayed in fastboot, try b left it and Android came back on slot b with slot a flagged unbootable; our kernel's life is not known yet
question: What did the Pixel 2 do when given the builder's first boot images with fastboot boot, and what did it leave behind?
found:
Try a (boot-a.img, taimen offsets): sent, the phone stayed in fastboot, no USB event on the host for 60 s. Try b (boot-b.img, LineageOS offsets): image accepted, "Booting" then the phone left USB at once; 20 s later it was Android's adb gadget (18d1:4ee7), Android on slot b (an older LineageOS build than slot a's), boot reason reboot,ota. Nothing of ours answered: no serial port, no RNDIS/ECM, 172.16.42.1 silent, pstore empty. Whether our kernel ran is not known yet.
The bootloader's A/B logic changed the state, with no write command from us: after try b the phone reports current-slot b and slot a unbootable = yes (first look: slot a current, unbootable no). Slot a's Android is presumably intact; restoring the flags is `set_active a`, a write that needs a recorded decision and the author's word. devlab called try b "refused", though the host log shows the phone left fastboot; it should read slot flags before and after a try and say what changed. Until the author decides about the slot flags no further try should be made.

brief: Why a failed fastboot boot flipped the Pixel 2's slots, how to restore, how to keep tries from flipping them
question: Why did two fastboot boot tries change the A/B state, how do we restore it, how do we keep tries from flipping it, and should tries run on slot b?
found:
Probable, not proven: the Pixel 2's bootloader is Qualcomm-derived ABL (Google's build is not public). In Qualcomm's ABL source (CAF pie mirror, QcomModulePkg FastbootCmds.c, PartitionTableUpdate.c, avb/VerifiedBoot.c), `fastboot boot` runs LoadImageAndAuth on the active slot; when that fails, HandleActiveSlotUnbootable sets slot a's unbootable flag (leaving successful set - the odd pair we saw), makes b active because b is successful, and cold-resets before the reply (our "Status read failed"). So our kernel probably never ran, and panic=10 is not the cause. `fastboot boot` does not decrement retry-count; a kernel crash falls back to a normal boot of the stock boot partition; a slot that is successful=yes is never counted down.
set_active X (ABL source): makes the slot active at priority 3, retry 7, clears unbootable and successful; swaps the a/b partition-type GUIDs and switches the UFS boot LUN: metadata only, undone by set_active back. a stays successful=no until Android on a marks itself good. `--slot` is ignored by `boot`.
Pixel 2 reports: loops end in "Slot Unbootable: Load Error", fixed by set_active (UBports forum 5639); after 7 unsuccessful boots the bootloader switches slot (pmaports MR 3190); the Pixel 2 XL bootloader refuses a kernel unless dtbo holds overlay id 2704 (kcxt dtbo README) - the likely real cause of the failed authentication, unconfirmed for walleye.
Not known yet: the real failure point; why try a stayed in fastboot and whether it changed flags; why b shows retry 0 after the switch; whether Google's ABL matches Qualcomm's.
Ways: leave flags and try on b (no write; if b is flagged too, set_active is the way out); set_active a now (a stays successful=no, the next failed try flips again); set_active before each try (a write per try); flash a stub dtbo to the active slot (a write, no known way back: the stock dtbo cannot be read back by fastboot); image changes (os_version 0 in our header untested).

brief: Public sources: walleye/taimen boot.img is header v0, base 0, page 4096; no dtb/dtbo fields in v0; os_version is set by the AOSP build, not by porthole's deviceinfo
question: What do LineageOS's wahoo build and porthole's mkbootimg inputs say about header version, page size, base and os_version, and does a v0 header fit walleye?
found: LineageOS wahoo (lineage-15.1 BoardConfig.mk): BOARD_KERNEL_BASE 0, PAGESIZE 4096, default kernel offset, tags 0x01E00000 and ramdisk 0x02000000 for walleye and muskie (0x80000/0x02500000/0x02700000 only for the kasan builds), no header-version, dtb or recovery_dtbo argument: header v0; BOARD_USES_RECOVERY_AS_BOOT and system-as-root, dtbo in its own partition. Porthole's taimen deviceinfo: header v0, base 0, kernel 0x8000, ramdisk 0x1000000, tags 0x100, pagesize 4096 'verified against the stock taimen boot.img', kernel with the dtb appended, dtbo flashed to its own partition, no os_version set. A v0 header has no dt size or recovery_dtbo field (those arrive with v1/v2), so v0 fits walleye as far as public sources say; walleye's own stock header is still not read. The two offset sets are the two publics': taimen's stock (a) and LineageOS's (b), and try a, with the stock offsets, did not leave fastboot while b did. os_version/patch level: the AOSP build writes them into every boot.img (PLATFORM_VERSION, PLATFORM_SECURITY_PATCH); no public source for walleye gives the value, so variants c and d use 8.1.0 / 2020-01 (a pick). Not known: whether ABL reads them, and whether the dtbo overlay id (backlog walleye-dtbo-overlay-id) or the signature/AVB footer decides instead; porthole flashes a stub dtbo, which we have not.

brief: Second tries on slot b: boot-a accepted (Booting OKAY) but not started, boot-b refused (Load Error); slot flags did not change; our kernel still not seen
question: What do boot-a.img and boot-b.img do with slot b active, with devlab's before/after slot report?
found:
With b active (a unbootable, as left): try a - fastboot "Booting OKAY [0.052s]", the phone stays in fastboot, no USB event, nothing answers. Try b - "Booting FAILED (remote: 'Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error')", stays in fastboot. Slot flags before and after were identical both times (current b; a unbootable yes, successful yes; b unbootable no, successful yes; retry-counts 0), so set-active was not needed and was not used; nothing written.
The first try b (17:37, slot a active) behaved differently: the phone left USB and Android came up on b with a flagged unbootable. Same image, so what decided is not known yet (the active slot, or something that changed in between). Our kernel has not been seen to start at all. Next: the builder's variant with os_version and patch level set; a dtbo stub stays the author's decision.

brief: boot-c and boot-d (os_version and patch level set): both refused with Load Error, phone stays in fastboot, no USB event, flags unchanged; no image has started our kernel
question: Does setting os_version and patch level in the header make the bootloader start our boot image?
found:
Try c (boot-a plus the header os word) and try d (boot-b plus it), on slot b with devlab's before/after report: both fastboot "Booting FAILED (remote: 'Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error')" after the 0.368 s transfer. The phone stayed in fastboot: 18d1:4ee0 in all 90 one-second lsusb polls after each, nothing new on USB (no Linux gadget, no serial port), host kernel log empty. Slot flags identical before and after (current b, a unbootable). No write, no set-active.
So the os_version/patch level word does not make the bootloader accept our images, and it turned boot-a's silent "Booting OKAY" into a Load Error. No image has started our kernel; what the loader dislikes (header, kernel format, dtb, missing dtbo) is not known yet. Open: a dtbo stub is a write and stays the author's decision; the builder may try other header fields or a kernel with the dtb as Android expects.

brief: Walleye's stock boot.img (LineageOS 22.2 20261113): header v0, offsets as our image a, one dtb with msm-id 0x124/0x20001 and no board-id/pmic-id; ids are in the dtbo table
question: What do walleye's stock boot header and dtb carry (page size, offsets, cmdline, os word, qcom,msm-id/board-id/pmic-id), and is a dtbo present?
found: Source: LineageOS official walleye boot.img, build 20261113, https://mirrorbits.lineageos.org/full/walleye/20261113/boot.img, 33554432 bytes, sha256 48dbc55c76ee47840e645707b6bf3ac322099c06358178ad8ddf2c6a53c17468 (equals the site's published value; kept at ~/Projects/walleye-build/control/boot.img, data only, never run on the host). download.lineageos.org publishes no recovery.img for walleye; on A/B the recovery is in boot. unpack_bootimg: header v0; page size 4096; kernel load 0x8000; ramdisk 0x1000000; second size 0 and address 0; tags 0x100 (base 0: taimen/blueline offsets, the same as our image a); os_version 15.0.0, os_patch_level 2026-11 (a nonzero os word; ours are 0, or 8.1.0/2020-01 in c,d); product name empty; cmdline: androidboot.hardware=walleye androidboot.console=ttyMSM0 lpm_levels.sleep_disabled=1 user_debug=31 msm_rtb.filter=0x37 ehci-hcd.park=3 service_locator.enable=1 swiotlb=2048 firmware_class.path=/vendor/firmware loop.max_part=7 raid=noautodetect usbcore.autosuspend=7 androidboot.dtbo_idx=3. Kernel: lz4 (sha256 0256983d1002752214fde5035f78ce07e088d167bad993f3f16e1e9f78162872), Linux 4.4.302 arm64, with ONE dtb appended at byte 17613814 (376259 bytes, sha256 37dd8612cab84bd96025bd5831eac194fcf1f10bc8f8f08ea6ff72717a8f5751): model 'Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. MSM8998 v2.1', compatible qcom,msm8998-mtp / qcom,msm8998 / qcom,mtp, qcom,msm-id <0x124 0x20001>; NO qcom,board-id and NO qcom,pmic-id at the root. Ramdisk is xz (sha256 a0d50bc3063f3fd60e93c067ca9b54d16e670b6171eb498decc294d658f5dcbf). So the stock dtb is matched on msm-id alone, as ours is. The board identity is in the dtbo: dtbo.img of the same build (8388608 bytes, sha256 fb09009b7946bf33d860ee94cadfabdfcf3cf63a872314bc650d9220486bb8f6, equals the site's) holds a DT table of 13 entries, ids 0x1bc (revs 0-4 and 0x80), 0x190, 0x490, 0x590, 0x690 and more; androidboot.dtbo_idx=3 names the one merged; the overlays carry no qcom,board-id. So variant f's premise (stock board-id/pmic-id to copy) does not hold: f adds qcom,board-id <8 0> only (what qcom,mtp means), a guess, no pmic-id.

brief: Control boot.img on slot a: Load Error again; the slot state is not the cause. Phone back on b, fastboot reachable
question: Does the LineageOS control boot.img boot by fastboot boot with slot a active (the state of the very first tries)?
found: No. Per decision walleye-slot-set-active-a-once: devlab fastboot set-active now a (before: current b, a unbootable yes/successful yes/retry 0, b unbootable no/successful yes/retry 0; after: current a, a unbootable no/successful no/retry 1). devlab fastboot boot now control/boot.img (sha256 48dbc55c..., LineageOS 22.2 20261113): 'Sending boot.img OKAY', then 'Booting FAILED (remote: Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error)'; still in fastboot after a minute; the try changed no flags. So the refusal is not caused by slot b being active or by a being flagged unbootable: the same stock image is refused on a too. Open causes: dtbo/vbmeta state (a write, the author's or coordinator's call), or fastboot boot on this bootloader never takes an image of this kind. Restored with set-active now b: current b, a unbootable no/successful no/retry 1, b unbootable no/successful no/retry 1 (set-active resets b's successful flag; both slots bootable, retry counts 1); fastboot reachable, nothing written.

brief: Load Error is not the slot flags (control refused on a too); the one accepted try came with healthy Android on a, so the next test restores that state, then cold restart, host checks, UART
question: Why does the Pixel 2's bootloader refuse even LineageOS's official boot.img by fastboot boot (Load Error), and what makes fastboot boot work on it?
found:
What is: the control (LineageOS 22.2 20261113 boot.img, stock header, AVB footer, own dtb) is refused with "Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error" on slot b and, per walleye-control-on-slot-a-try, on slot a too; so are our b-f. Seen to be accepted: our boot-b on the very first try (slot a active, phone entered fastboot from healthy Android): the phone left USB, Android came up on b, a flagged unbootable; and boot-a, "Booting OKAY" with nothing starting, on slot b. The same image was refused later. So the refusal is not the image's format and, after the slot-a try, not the active slot or the unbootable flag alone. The same string and A/B flip are reported for walleye since 2017 (XDA PSA); on other Qualcomm ABL phones it comes "randomly" and goes with a restart, another port or cable, set_active or a stock reflash.

Ranked causes now (each by what it predicts):
1. State left by the first tries that set_active does not undo. The one accepted try came from a phone booted into Android on a, with a successful=yes (Android marks it when boot completes). Now a is successful=no, retry 1, and b's flag was reset by our set-active (b successful no). Predicts: after Android boots on a to completion (marks it successful) and the phone is put into the bootloader from that Android, the control is accepted again. Cheapest and reversible; it is the exact first state. Not tested.
2. A bootloader that has stayed up since a failed boot (the 'restart cures it' reports). Predicts: a cold power-off and start into the bootloader, then the same try, is accepted. Not tested; also covered by 1, which reboots the phone.
3. dtbo (or vbmeta) of the active slot. The bootloader picks overlays from dtbo by id and rev and refuses if none fits (AOSP DTO; the taimen bootloader wants id 2704, kcxt). Slot b's is an older Lineage build's and a's is current, yet both refuse, so a mismatch with the new dtb is unlikely; a cause only if 1 and 2 fail. A write; stays named, with no way back for the stock dtbo (fastboot cannot read it back).
4. Host: old fastboot, USB port, cable. The transfer succeeds and the refusal comes back at "booting", so least likely; recorded with each try (fastboot --version).
5. AVB and lock state: the phone reports unlocked yes, where verification errors are warnings; not measured.

Not known yet: the bootloader's own reason. Google's ABL is not public (the CAF Qualcomm ABL only shows the shape) and fastboot has no read-only oem command that prints it. The way to see it is the serial log over the Pixel 2's Android Debug Cable (Nura wiki), which needs the author's hardware.

Vector chosen: restore the first state, since it is the only state in which an image was accepted: set-active a, boot Android on a normally to completion (a's own Android, nothing written), adb reboot bootloader, the control once; then, if still refused, cold power-off start and host checks; then UART; a write last.

brief: First state restored: control ACCEPTED by fastboot boot after Android completed on a; phone then left USB entirely (no adb/fastboot) - needs a hand power-cycle
question: Does restoring the first state (Android completed on slot a, adb reboot bootloader) make the bootloader accept the control boot.img?
found: Yes. set-active a, fastboot reboot, Android up on a (sys.boot_completed 1, slot _a). After adb reboot bootloader: current-slot a, a unbootable no/successful yes/retry 0, b unbootable no/successful no/retry 1. devlab fastboot boot now control/boot.img: left fastboot after 12 s. devlab's 'came back as Linux, USB network answering' is a false match: the 18d1:d001 gadget (Qualcomm SM7150, serial postmarketOS) on the bus is the surya phone; walleye FA81N1A00790 was on no USB, no adb, no fastboot for 6+ min. So cause 1 (state left by the first tries) is confirmed: Load Error follows the slot's successful flag, not the image. Nothing written. The lab has no power control for walleye, so it is not back in fastboot: a hand hold of power 10-30 s is needed (slot a is successful, so it boots Android on a; then adb reboot bootloader). Next: boot-b/e from the same first state; fix devlab's came-back check to match the manifest serial.

brief: e and b accepted from the first state, neither started: no USB device, flags unchanged, phone stays in fastboot
question: Does fastboot boot of our images e and b start from the restored first state?
found: Both ACCEPTED (Booting OKAY) but not started: 90 s watch by serial, phone stays in fastboot, no new USB device, no 172.16.42.1 (172.16.42.2 is surya's), slot flags unchanged; acceptance is not the cause of silence

brief: s1 (our gadget ramdisk), s2 (our kernel), s3 (our dtb) tried from the first state: none started; s1 and s2 fell back to stock Android on a, s3 accepted but stayed in fastboot
question: Which stock part, swapped for ours, makes walleye's bootloader stop starting the image?
found: From the first state (current-slot a, a successful, b unbootable), no writes. s1: left fastboot after 12 s, Android on slot _a kernel 4.4.302 after 75 s, no 172.16.43.1, no new USB device (only the stock adb): our gadget did NOT come up; stock vendor kernel/dtb/cmdline with our ramdisk did not start (a stock boot of slot a is what ran). s2: same shape (12 s, Android on a, 4.4.302 after 72 s). s3: 'Booting OKAY' then stayed in fastboot, no USB event. Flags unchanged each time (a successful, b unbootable). Together with s0n (no start) and s0 (stock with AVB footer, accepted earlier): every image that differs from the stock footer-carrying boot.img, even ramdisk only, fails to start; s0n shows the footer or padding alone may be enough. Next: rebuild s1 with the AVB footer (algorithm NONE, padded to 32 MiB like s0) and try it.

brief: s1 = vendor-gadget image (footer, 32 MiB) refused with Load Error on slot a twice; gadget-up fails; earlier s1/s2 'left fastboot' were fallbacks to stock a
question: Does the stock kernel with our gadget initramfs (s1, AVB footer present, size 33554432 checked) start from the first state, and does 172.16.43.1 answer?
found: Checked: boot-s0/s1/s2/s3 are 33554432 bytes and end in AVBf; s0n is 26472448 without. Then, current-slot a (a successful, b unbootable yes retry 1): devlab fastboot boot now boot-s1.img -> 'Failed to load/authenticate boot image: Load Error', flags unchanged; again with images/vendor-gadget.img (same bytes) while GADGET_WAIT=90 gadget-up.sh (from the builder's worktree wt-walleye-builder-lab, not yet landed in the lab) ran: same Load Error, gadget-up: fail, no USB device with our strings, 2 google devices (the phone in fastboot and surya?). The earlier s1/s2 runs this session (left fastboot after 12 s, Android on a 4.4.302) were therefore fallbacks to stock, not starts; my earlier suggestion to rebuild s1 with the footer was wrong - it has it. Earlier research showed Load Error followed the slot state; b is unbootable now and tries have been run with a active this time, so the open question is whether the state (b unbootable, active a) or the image causes it. No write.

brief: s1 boots the stock kernel (bootreason kernel_panic, back on a after 75 s); the vendor kernel has no ACM/ECM/RNDIS, only NCM and FunctionFS, no devtmpfs - our gadget init cannot show up on it
question: What did the s1 try do, and what does the running vendor kernel offer our gadget init?
found: Bootloader first: after the earlier Load Errors both slots ended unbootable (a: unbootable yes, retry 0) and the phone stayed in fastboot after a reboot; one metadata-only 'devlab fastboot set-active now a' cleared a (unbootable no, successful no, retry 1) and Android completed on a (successful yes again). s1 re-run from that healthy first state: left fastboot after 12 s, Android on a after 75 s, ro.boot.bootreason=kernel_panic - so the stock kernel DID start with our ramdisk and panicked, then the bootloader fell back to a. (Load Error appeared only when run from the state after several refusals.) Facts, read-only from the vendor kernel 4.4.302 (adb root, debuggable): UDC a800000.dwc3. Config: USB_CONFIGFS=y, F_FS, NCM, MASS_STORAGE, MTP, PTP, ACC, AUDIO_SRC, MIDI, HID, DIAG, GSI, CDEV, QDSS = y; ACM, SERIAL, OBEX, ECM, RNDIS, EEM are NOT set; DEVTMPFS not set; PSTORE, PSTORE_CONSOLE, PSTORE_PMSG, PSTORE_RAM, ACCESS_RAMOOPS = y. Our gadget init (ACM + RNDIS/ECM) therefore could not bring up a gadget on this kernel even if init ran; it needs NCM (host sees a cdc_ncm interface) and, with no devtmpfs, mounting devtmpfs fails - our init must mknod or use mdev. Ramoops: ramoops_region reg 0xa1100000 size 0x200000; alt_ramoops_region 0xa3800000 size 0x200000; meta region 0xaffff000 size 0x1000; params record 524288, console 262144? (from /sys/module/ramoops: mem_size 2097152, record 524288, console 131072 order as listed). The pstore is encrypted by vendor ramoops (init.ramoops.sh: ramoops -D after the user unlocks, files appear in /data/vendor_ce/0/ramoops, absent here), so the s1 panic text is NOT readable from Android; /sys/fs/pstore empty. Cmdline of the vendor boot: androidboot.hardware=walleye console=ttyMSM0 ... root=PARTUUID, androidboot.dtbo_idx=3, panel mdss_dsi_samsung_s6e3fa5_1080p_cmd, serial redacted. Next: rebuild s1's init for NCM (+ mknod, no devtmpfs), keep the panic hunt by making init print to /dev/kmsg-less console only if needed; or make our init never exit (sleep loop) to see if the panic was init exiting.

brief: The 60 s panic: check the system-as-root cmdline (free, read-only) first, then the panic time, then ramoops after the author's unlock; UART is the sure route
question: Why does the vendor 4.4.302 kernel panic about 60 s after fastboot boot with our ramdisk, and how can the panic text be read?
found: WHAT IS (lab base): the vendor 4.4.302 kernel started with our swapped ramdisk (xz, so not the gzip fault) and panics before any gadget: bootreason kernel_panic, USB gone at ~12 s, Android back on a at 68-74 s; the true panic time is NOT measured (the host sees USB only, and the fallback Android boot itself takes tens of seconds, so the panic may be at ~30-60 s, not 60). Stock-kernel pstore is empty from Android (vendor ramoops -D encrypts after unlock). CAUSES, ranked by what the facts support, each with the one cheap try that tells it apart. (1) Our ramdisk is not what runs: Pixel 2 is system-as-root (A/B, recovery in boot; LineageOS flashes recovery into boot), and a system-as-root cmdline is ro root=/dev/dm-0 rootwait skip_initramfs init=/init - the kernel then ignores the boot ramdisk and runs /init from the system partition (src-android-system-as-root); a bootloader can add skip_initramfs itself (src-magisk-skip-initramfs). Then our /init never ran, which fits no gadget ever, and the later panic is Android first-stage failing on a half-set-up boot. Told apart by two READ-ONLY facts: the full /proc/cmdline and /proc/device-tree/chosen/bootargs of the running Android (skip_initramfs, root=, dm=), and the control image header cmdline (host, from the file). Needs no try. If skip_initramfs is there, gadget4 (idle init) is moot for the panic and the way is an image whose cmdline/ABL path honours our ramdisk, or the system partition route; this goes first because it is free. (2) A kernel-side failure independent of userspace: a peripheral (modem/adsp/slpi via PIL) crashing or timing out with restart level SYSTEM prints subsys-restart ... Resetting the SoC and panics (src-qcom-log-analysis); the user-mode firmware fallback waits 60 s by default (src-kernel-firmware-fallback), so a missing userspace ueventd can turn into a panic about a minute in. Told apart by gadget4 (idle init that survives): the same gap with an idle init means kernel-side; the cheaper first step is to measure the panic time (see below). (3) Our init exiting or crashing: ruled out in time by gadget3 (240 s timer, no early exit seen), and gadget4 tests it again. (4) MSM apps watchdog: pet by the kernel, not userspace, so unlikely; reads as watchdog bark/bite in the text. HOW TO READ THE PANIC TEXT, cheapest first: (a) Measure the time instead of reading the text: a 1 s USB watcher over a plain adb reboot gives T_android (USB loss to Android on USB); the panic try gives the gap; panic time = gap - T_android. This needs no write. 60 s plus ~12 s would point at the firmware fallback; ~25-45 s at an early kernel fault. (b) Previous boot text in ramoops: region 0xa1100000 2 MiB is reserved, so the panic text survives the warm reset (src-kernel-ramoops-doc) but the vendor init consumes and encrypts it into /data/vendor_ce/0/ramoops once the user unlocks; so after a panic try, boot Android on a, have the author unlock the phone once (credential is the author, not ours), and read the ramoops files as root - UNKNOWN whether the file appears for a non-user-initiated reboot: one try shows it. The phone must not be rebooted again before reading, or the next boot overwrites the buffer. (c) Our own ramdisk as reader: only if (1) is false - a second try image whose init mounts pstore and only prints to a path we can read; no channel exists, so not first. (d) UART: the Android Debug Cable (USB-C passthrough breakout + FT232 TTL, a purchase of a few euros for the author, src-pixel-uart-cable) works on walleye (src-nura-serial-pixel2); fastboot oem uart enable needs the unlocked bootloader (it is) and is a bootloader setting that persists until fastboot oem uart disable - a write with a way back; the 1.8 V line needs the board to be right. It gives the bootloader log AND the kernel console to the end of the panic, so it answers causes 1-4 at once and also the Load Error question; it is the sure route, kept second only because it costs a purchase and a hand. (e) /proc/last_kmsg: not in 4.4 Android (moved to console-ramoops, Android 6+). (f) Not now: kernel rebuild with the earlycon/pstore console to the cmdline, a dtbo write.

brief: ncm panic: our init writes dev_addr/host_addr on the ncm function while opts->net is still NULL (net is made at UDC bind); mkdir and symlink are not the cause
question: Why does the ncm function (or its config symlink) panic the vendor msm-4.4 kernel, and which function is safe and gives a channel?
found: Ranked causes. 1 (source-proven, not yet counted on the phone): the two `echo > functions/ncm.usb0/{dev_addr,host_addr}` lines in every gadget init (vendor, 3, 5b, 5c). In the wahoo 4.4 tree ncm_alloc_inst leaves opts->net NULL (the net_device is made in ncm_bind at UDC bind) and refcnt is 0 until the symlink, so the attribute store calls gether_set_dev_addr(NULL,...): NULL deref, oops, panic. After the symlink the store returns -EBUSY, so no write is ever valid here. Fits all facts: 5a (no function) and gadget4 return; 5b and gadget2/3 panic; mkdir and symlink alone do not touch net (ncm_alloc only refcnt++). 2: the UDC bind (ncm_bind -> gether_register_netdev, dwc3 endpoints) could panic in 5c; unknowable until 1 is removed (Android never uses ncm: its stack is gsi/ffs, so the vendor never exercised this path). 3: the symlink itself: no code path touches net; unlikely. Safe alternatives, with the image that tells: (a) ncm WITHOUT any attribute write (random MACs; set the device side later with ip link set usb0 address): image ncm-noattr = 5c minus the two echo lines; returns at 120 s with no panic and the host sees our strings = confirmed. (b) ffs with a tiny static aarch64 helper: more work, no gain if (a) works; the fallback. (c) gsi.rndis/rmnet: need IPA driver and firmware at early init, not a first channel. (d) mass_storage read-only image: host sees a disk, no log stream; crude fallback. (e) mtp/ptp/acc: need a userspace daemon; no. Caveat: the source is the public android11 branch of the wahoo 4.4 line; the phone runs 4.4.302, the exact build is not public, so the image is the proof.

brief: FunctionFS cannot carry CDC functional descriptors, but cdc_acm binds one class-2 interface with 3 endpoints: the helper declares that, writes ep0 before the UDC bind, bridges to a pty shell
question: How can FunctionFS give the host a /dev/ttyACM0 with a shell, on the vendor 4.4.302 kernel (ACM/SERIAL/ECM/RNDIS off, F_FS on, no devtmpfs), from a tiny static aarch64 C helper?
found:
What is: the running kernel is the stock 4.4.302 with our ramdisk (research walleye-vendor-kernel-facts-s1-panic): USB_CONFIGFS and F_FS =y, ACM/SERIAL/ECM/RNDIS not set, no devtmpfs, UDC a800000.dwc3. Android itself uses ffs.adb in configfs group g1 on this phone (src-wahoo-init-hardware-usb-rc), so F_FS is exercised by the stock stack.

Finding 1 (the trap): f_fs's descriptor parser (v4.4.302 and v7.3 alike) rejects any descriptor type outside interface, endpoint, HID, OTG, interface-association and SS-companion; CS_INTERFACE (0x24, the CDC header/call-management/ACM/union descriptors) falls to default -> -EINVAL. The queued idea of declaring the full CDC functional descriptors would make the write to ep0 fail.

Finding 2 (the way): cdc_acm's probe, with no union descriptor and a class 2 / subclass 2 / protocol 1 interface with exactly three endpoints, assumes a single combined interface and picks interrupt-in, bulk-in, bulk-out with usb_find_common_endpoints. So ONE interface (class 0x02, sub 0x02, proto 0x01) with interrupt-in (10 bytes, interval 9), bulk-out and bulk-in (512 HS/SS, 64 FS) plus SS companion descriptors is enough; the host gives /dev/ttyACM0. Line coding / control-line-state are best-effort for the host.

Design: (1) init: mount configfs; gadget with ids and strings as n2; functions/ffs.acm, configs/c.1 symlink; mkdir /dev/ffs; mount -t functionfs acm /dev/ffs (no devtmpfs: nodes by cpio; ep0 appears in the ffs mount, ep1..3 after the descriptors are written; /dev/ptmx a cpio node, mount devpts). (2) helper (C, static aarch64, clang, GPL base ffs-test.c, libc only): open /dev/ffs/ep0; write the V2 descriptors blob (flags FS|HS|SS), then the strings blob (lang 0x0409); only then write the UDC name (before that the configfs bind returns -ENODEV: f_fs desc_ready). (3) ep0 loop: on ENABLE open ep1..ep3 (names follow descriptor order) and fork a pty shell (posix_openpt, /bin/sh as session leader); on DISABLE/UNBIND close and kill; answer class SETUP events (SET_LINE_CODING 0x20, GET_LINE_CODING 0x21, SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE 0x22) with a zero-length ack or canned 115200 8N1 so cdc_acm sees no stall; any other setup gets a stall. (4) bridge: poll pty master and ep2 (bulk-out) -> ep3 (bulk-in); ep1 opened and idle. A bulk-in write blocks until the host reads, so use a thread or timeout so a missing host never hangs the shell; log to /dev/kmsg only on state changes. (5) the mass-storage log window stays the second channel.

Failure modes and how each looks: UDC write ENODEV (descriptors not written first, or parse -EINVAL: helper reports errno on /dev/kmsg and the mass-storage window); enumerates but no ttyACM (host cdc_acm rejected: host dmesg); enumerates then drops (ep0 events unanswered: host reset); panic (as 5b, an unwritten function attribute: this design writes no function attribute, only ep0 data) - the bootloader falls back to slot a as before.

Not measured yet: whether the vendor's f_fs (Android common 4.4 plus patches) behaves like stock 4.4.302 here (read, not run); the host side of the ACM bind.

brief: Our dtb has no __symbols__; the dtbo overlay (idx 3) needs 137 labels, so it cannot merge: fdtoverlay fails on ours, passes on stock. Fits s3 'Booting OKAY' then fastboot.
question: Does the bootloader's dtbo overlay merge need __symbols__ and the nodes the overlays patch, and is that why our dtb is never started?
found:
What is: androidboot.dtbo_idx=3 (set by the bootloader) = dtbo.img entry 3 (id 0x1bc rev 3), 147 fragments, label-targeted, __fixups__ naming 137 labels of the base dtb (cci, tlmm, soc, mdss_mdp, pm8998_gpios...). No msm-id/board-id in the overlays; the entry is picked by id/rev, then merged into the dtb of the boot image.
Measured on the host (material: dtbo-measurements.md): fdtoverlay merges entry 3 into the stock dtb (986 symbols, all 137 present) and FAILS on ours: no /__symbols__ node. AOSP's libufdt, the reference for Android's overlay merge, treats that as an error (aosp-libufdt-overlay). Even compiled with -@, our dtb would carry about 14 of the 137 labels (mainline names), and its soc is soc@0, so the fixups would still not resolve.
Fits the bisect: s0n/s0 (stock dtb) start; s2 (our kernel, stock dtb) starts the kernel and falls back; s3 (our dtb, stock kernel) alone reaches 'Booting OKAY' then stays in fastboot - the only variant whose dtb cannot take the overlay. So the dtbo merge is the likeliest cause of s3, and one that outlives every later fix: the vendor ABL will overlay any dtb we hand it. Not known yet: what Google's ABL does on a failed merge (its source is not public; libufdt returns an error, ABL may refuse or continue) - the one cheap image tells.
Does not explain the Load Error of the control (stock dtb merges fine): that stays on research walleye-boot-refused-why-how-it-stands.
Ways: (a) give our dtb the symbols: a compatibility dtsi with stub nodes for the ~123 missing labels, built with -@ - host-testable by fdtoverlay, but adds vendor stubs the mainline kernel ignores; (b) boot the stock dtb for first light and move to ours later - the kernel then runs on the vendor dtb, wrong for mainline drivers; (c) patch the stock dtb: replace its nodes with ours - same merge-safety, much larger; (d) remove the overlay from the path: only by writing dtbo (a write, not proposed); (e) ask the bootloader to skip it: no known way (androidboot.dtbo_idx is its output, not input).
Chosen: (a), narrowed: generate the stub label set from the overlay's own __fixups__ (the 137 names, each with the path it has in the stock dtb's __symbols__), build with -@, prove with tests/host/dtbo-overlay-merges.sh on the host first, then one image on the phone.

found: boot-ml3.img (sha256 5c257470...) booted from the first state with fastboot boot: left fastboot after 15 s, USB light never (no walleye-first-boot device), Android on slot a after 72 s, androidboot.bootreason=reboot. adb root works (Lineage-like build). Android's ramoops is at mem_address 2702180352 = 0xa1100000, size 2 MiB, record 524288, console 131072, pmsg 0 - it matches our node. /sys/fs/pstore has 0 files, no 'no valid data' line; /data/vendor_ce/0/ramoops holds only pub/priv pem. So no console record of ours: either our kernel dies before the pstore console registers, or the reset clears DDR (a bootloader/PMIC reset, not a warm one - bootreason is plain reboot, not kernel_panic/watchdog). Together with ml1/ml2 the 7.3 image has never shown a sign of life.

brief: n3r enumerates, cdc_acm refuses it: 'Zero length descriptor references' (-22); cdc_acm needs at least one class-specific descriptor on the interface
question: Why does the host not bind cdc_acm to the FunctionFS single-interface console of n3r?
found: n3r tried once on slot b (set-active b, fastboot boot): the gadget came up as 1d6b:0104 'Pixel 2 walleye (mainline)' serial walleye-first-boot, one class-2 interface. Host dmesg: 'cdc_acm 3-2:1.0: Zero length descriptor references; probe failed with error -22'. In acm_probe the interface extra bytes (and the first endpoint's extra) are empty, so it returns -EINVAL before the union-descriptor fallback ('castrated device') is reached; that fallback only works when some extra descriptor exists. Fix to try: write a CDC header functional descriptor (plus call-management and ACM, no union required) after the interface descriptor in the FunctionFS descriptors. Contradicts the wording of decision walleye-ffs-acm-single-interface (no CDC functional descriptors), so it goes to the coordinator.

brief: Empty pstore after mainline tries is not yet evidence of a cold reset: no try showed a kernel alive; and mainline never asks the PMIC for a warm reset the way the vendor kernel does
question: Why does our mainline kernel's console never survive in pstore, and how does an MSM8998 kernel ask for a warm reset so ramoops at 0xa1100000 keeps its text?
found: READ FROM SOURCE. (1) Vendor wahoo 4.4 msm_restart_prepare: the PMIC reset type is set explicitly before every restart; WARM only if download mode is on (in_panic turns it on) or the reboot command is non-empty ('reboot recovery'); a plain reboot is a PMIC HARD reset ('unless memory contents must be maintained'). It then de-asserts PS_HOLD through TZ. So on the phone, only panics and 'reboot <arg>' keep DDR; this is why stock Android's console-ramoops survives a panic but not a plain reboot. (2) Mainline: reboot=w sets REBOOT_WARM, but psci_sys_reset uses SYSTEM_RESET2 only if PSCI is 1.1+; otherwise plain SYSTEM_RESET (notifier priority 129, before qcom-wdt's 128, so the watchdog restart is never reached). The pm8998-pon driver only registers reboot-mode (soft spare reason) and never programs the PS_HOLD warm/hard reset type. Nothing in mainline does what msm_restart_prepare does; panic=5 and sysrq c therefore end in the same plain reset, whatever the PMIC default is (set by SBL/XBL: not known yet). (3) The lab's tries (ml1-ml5, pk*) never showed a kernel alive (no USB, no earlycon on the host), so an empty pstore says nothing yet about warm or cold: ramoops registers at postcore, so a kernel that dies earlier, or never starts, leaves nothing. RANKED CAUSES: (A) no kernel code ran far enough to write (most likely for ml*; test: any sign of life first, e.g. the m1 mass-storage log); (B) plain reset = PMIC hard reset, DDR lost (certain to matter once A is cleared; mainline sets no reset type); (C) the reader: stock 4.4 ramoops layout/ECC/zone count differs from the 7.x writer's, or Android init consumes the files (read with adb root right after boot; compare the 4.4 and 7.x zone maths before trusting an empty read; the clean control is the SAME kernel reading its own region after a warm reset); (D) bootloader zeroes the region on a path other than a warm reset (not shown by anything; Pixel stock Android relies on survival after panic, so XBL/ABL keep DDR on the warm path). NOT TESTED: all of it; nothing here ran on the phone. CHEAP IMAGE CHANGES, each one image, expected pstore: (T1) init marker to /dev/kmsg, 20 s wait, 'echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger' with panic=5: console/dmesg-ramoops present only if the reset kept DDR; expected ABSENT (cause B). (T2) same, cmdline reboot=w added: expected the same, because PSCI on MSM8998 TZ is 1.0 as far as known (dmesg 'PSCIv' line to confirm) so no RESET2. (T3) init opens /dev/watchdog (kpss-wdt, already in the dts) with a short timeout and never pets it: a bite is a SoC watchdog reset which the vendor treats as a dump-capable warm path; expected console-ramoops PRESENT; this is the one image change with real hope and needs no kernel patch. (T4) kernel patch: a reboot notifier writing the PON PS_HOLD reset-type register to WARM (SPMI regmap of the pm8998 pon node; register and values to be read from the vendor qpnp-power-on source and header before writing) and arming it in the notifier; a patch worth sending upstream if T3 does not hold. READ-BACK WITHOUT PSTORE: after any return the PMIC's own record (PON_ON_REASON 0x40 = warm sequence, PON_WARM_RESET_REASON) tells which reset ran; stock Android exposes it in bootreason and in /sys/class/power_supply or qpnp pon sysfs; the live mass-storage log of init-pk5l (rewritten every 5 s) already gives the console without any pstore once a kernel is alive.

brief: arm-smmu 5040000 times out because gpucc is =m in a kernel whose initramfs has no modules
question: Why does arm-smmu 5040000 fail with -110 on our mainline kernel?
found: Mainline msm8998.dtsi gives adreno_smmu (iommu@5040000) power-domains = gpucc GPU_GX_GDSC; gpucc is node clock-controller@5065000. The kernel's .config has CONFIG_MSM_GPUCC_8998=m (Kconfig: default m), our initramfs carries no modules, so no driver ever binds gpucc, the GDSC never registers, and the smmu defers until the 11 s deferred-probe timeout (-110). The gcc line 'sync_state() pending due to 5040000.iommu and 5065000.clock-controller' in the first dmesg says the same. Not yet measured on the phone: image z2 (gpucc =y) is built to test it. The two other faults (serial@c16f000 waiting on the overlay stub clock_gcc, the overlay's four phandle lines) belong to nodes the stock dtbo overlay adds, not to our dts; they are the next images.
sources: research 2026-11-18-walleye-first-mainline-shell-map; linux v7.3 arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/msm8998.dtsi and drivers/clk/qcom/Kconfig (MSM_GPUCC_8998)

brief: The serial wait and the four 'could not find phandle' lines have one cause: the clock_gcc stub has no #clock-cells, so the kernel reads each clock ID as a phandle
question: Why does c16f000.serial wait on /vendor-overlay-stubs/clock_gcc, and what are the four OF: could not find phandle lines of the first mainline dmesg?
found: Raw dmesg (lab material mainline-shell-20261118-082300, lines 169-173): phandle numbers -1934992561 (i2c@c179000), -1480237014 (bt_wcn3990), -943313008 (serial@c16f000), -130129017 (mnh-sm) are the vendor clock ID words (0x8caa5b4f ...) of 'clocks = <&clock_gcc ID ...>' from the stock dtbo overlay entry 3 (its __fixups__ clock_gcc names those four users). Our stub clock_gcc is an empty node: no #clock-cells, so the kernel takes the ID cell as a phandle. The serial's supplier is the stub, which never probes. Pointing /__symbols__/clock_gcc at /soc@0/clock-controller@100000 (gcc, #clock-cells 1) makes the merge write gcc's phandle (37) into all four; tests/host/overlay-clock-gcc.sh was seen failing on z2's dtb (306, the stub) and passes on z3's.

brief: PMIC bite power-off: qcom-pon is not the cause; vendor never sets the WD S2 type; only a register read settles which of three causes
question: What reset type does the PM8998 watchdog bite perform and why did z9's bite power the phone off?
found:
Question: what reset type does the PM8998 S2 stage (the watchdog's bite) perform, and why did z9's bite power the phone off?
Read from sources (no phone touched):
1. Hypothesis (b) of the coordinator, "qcom-pon overwrote the type", is ruled out: mainline qcom-pon.c v7.3 writes only 0x8f (soft reboot spare) and populates children; it never writes 0x56, 0x5a, 0x5b or 0x57.
2. The series writes S2_CTL (0x56) = 0x07 (HARD) at probe, plain write. The vendor kernel (walleye's own GPL driver) never writes 0x56 at all: it toggles only the WD enable bit in S2_CTL2 (0x57). The vendor's reset type for PS_HOLD goes through 0x5A (type) / 0x5B (enable, on gen2) with enable cleared first and a 500 us wait, no SEC_ACCESS unlock. So the vendor leaves the WD S2 type to the PMIC default / the bootloader (PBS/SBL): what it is on walleye is not in any source, only in the register.
3. Type encodings agree: WARM 0x01, SHUTDOWN 0x04, HARD 0x07 (vendor header), same as the series' constants. HARD "resets the MSM and all PMIC peripherals", WARM "the MSM but not all PMIC peripherals". Whether a HARD reset ends in a restart on PM8998 depends on a power-on trigger after the rail cycle; the sources do not say, so a HARD type that powers the phone off with nothing to turn it back on is plausible (a hard reset is a power-off followed by a re-trigger; the 'z9 off the bus' fits a PMIC that cycled and did not re-trigger, but also fits one that restarted into a boot that never enumerated USB).
4. 'Off the USB bus' is not 'powered off': the record has no current, LED or screen evidence. The second boot the phone made (if any) would show as an slot change or a POFF reason; only a register read settles which.
So: three causes stay open (write did not take or read back wrong; HARD does not self-restart on this PMIC; it restarted into a boot with no USB). One cheap, safe phone read separates them and no bite is needed: read 0x56,0x57,0x5a,0x5b,0xc5 (and 0x54,0x55) before arming (the spmi regmap debugfs, if z9 has it, else a readback in the ramdisk's command loop). The reading also shows what the bootloader set before the series wrote 0x07 (read before the driver probes is impossible from Linux; read the value in an image without the series' write, i.e. z8's dtb with the wdt node disabled, or note that the probe write comes first).
Not proven by the bite: the series bites (it does: pmic-wdt-bites, 20 s); its reset type is a board/PMIC setting the series sets to HARD as its own default for pm8916 - the 'power off' is not the series' fault, but the series' hard-coded HARD is a board choice that should become a property (qcom,s2-reset-type style) or stay for pm8916 only: an upstream question once measured.

brief: c3 hang: the SoC never left the USB bus, so no reset ran; the only visible change from c2 is the charger probe; the way back is a restart gate and a PMIC-side deadman
question: Why does c3 (c2 + fw_devlink=permissive, charger probed) not restart where c2 did, and what restart path must be proved before an image that probes the charger is used for a long try?
found:
READ from the host journal, the c2 and c3 materials and Linux v7.3 source; nothing ran on the phone. MATERIAL: c2-host-journal.txt, c3-host-journal.txt (host `journalctl -k`, CET = Z+1).
FACTS. (1) c2 control: gadget 1d6b:0104 enumerated 14:40:17, USB disconnect 14:43:17 = exactly 180 s later (the init's own self-reboot: 90 beats of 2 s), Android (18d1:4ee7) back at 14:43:37. The same init (init-z6) and the same psci SYSTEM_RESET therefore work when the charger is deferred. (2) c3: enumerated 15:13:50, NO disconnect and no re-enumeration up to 15:42 (28+ min, device 65 still on the bus): the SoC never reset. So it is not a reboot loop (a loop shows disconnects), not a slow recovery like z9, and not 'a reset that came back wrong': nothing shows a reset was carried out. The init's 180 s self-reboot (due ~15:16:50) and the reader's reboot -f left no trace. The host's descriptors are cached, so the bus entry proves only that the USB pull-up is still on, not that the kernel answers. (3) The init is not the cause: the self-reboot is its own subshell, independent of the tty, and the identical init restarted c2. (4) c2 to c3 differs by (a) the charger probing, (b) fw_devlink=permissive. The dmesg diff (c2 vs c3) shows no new driver probe line besides the charger path (the rest is order, and the four 'sync_state() pending' lines of gcc that c3 lacks because no consumer is deferred any more); so (a) is the only visible change. (5) The smbx driver at probe (qcom_smbx.c smb_init_seq) writes: Type-C software control (the power-role mask is cleared although its comment says 'upstream facing port': UFP_EN_CMD is not set, so all role bits are 0), OTG_CFG, CHARGING_ENABLE_CMD, CHGR_CFG2, USBIN ICL options (USB51), AICL options (SUSPEND_ON_COLLAPSE cleared), pre/fast charge current (1 A cap), and its own watchdog off. It has no .shutdown, no .remove and no reboot notifier: nothing in the driver touches the reset path. c3's readings: type USB, online 1, status Full, voltage_now 0, current_now 0 (rradc gave no numbers). (6) Every reset this phone has is TZ's: psci 1.0 gives only SYSTEM_RESET (no RESET2); panic=5, reboot -f and sysrq b all end in that SMC; the kpss apps watchdog's bite is a secure-side path too and was never shown to restart this phone on its own (T3 came back as Android at 42 s, class 'alive', no marker; z9's PMIC watchdog bit and powered the phone OFF, needing hands). 'The watchdog did not bite' is therefore weak evidence: the apps wdt's bite is not proven to work here.
RANKED CAUSES (none tried). (A) The reset request stalls in TZ or the PMIC: the one thing that differs with the charger probed is the PMIC's own state (USBIN present; Type-C and charge registers written); TZ's SYSTEM_RESET programs the PMIC PON reset type over its own SPMI channel and de-asserts PS_HOLD; a wait there freezes the CPU in the SMC and, with the other CPUs stopped by the restart, leaves the USB pull-up on and the host with a silent device - exactly what is seen, and why neither watchdog helped. Needs a PMIC-side exit (hold Power ~15 s, the KPDPWR S3 reset: hands). (B) A kernel crash or hang in the charger IRQ or rradc path before the reset request, then panic=5 into the same stalled SMC; the reader's 16 answers were fine, so a late event (cable state change, AICL, bark IRQ) would be needed; open. (C) One of the Type-C role / OTG / ICL writes changes the PMIC so that a PS_HOLD reset is refused or held (charger-triggered power-on logic with an open role); a sub-case of A that the register bisect separates. REJECTED by the facts: the init blocked on a tty write (c2 same init), a slow z9-like recovery (z9 left the bus), a reboot loop (no disconnect), fw_devlink=permissive itself (no probe other than the charger appeared).
THE PSTORE can give nothing likely: a hang writes no record, and the author's power hold is a PMIC hard reset which loses DDR (research walleye-pstore-warm-reset-how-it-stands). Ask the keeper for `ls /sys/fs/pstore` once, free, but do not wait on it.
THE WAY BACK, in the order it can be proved (decision 2026-11-18-walleye-restart-gate-before-charger-try): (1) tests/host/restart-check.sh (new, host-side, from the host journal) is the gate: an image passes when the gadget leaves the bus within 200 s of enumerating; restart-selftest.sh proves it on the recorded c2 (pass) and c3 (fail) journals. (2) c5 = c4's dtb with the charger driver built as a module and NOT loaded: the control - proves c4's dtb change (tps61099 fixed regulator, pm8998 gpio 5) restarts; gate pass expected. (3) c6 = the same, the init loads the module 40 s after enumeration and the self-reboot stays at 180 s: if the gate fails here and (2) passed, the driver's probe is the cause (A or C); hands needed once. (4) only then bisect inside the driver by a module option that skips one smb_init_seq group at a time (Type-C, OTG, charging, ICL/AICL), each image gated. (5) The deadman that needs no TZ is the PMIC watchdog with S2 type HARD RESET (items walleye-pmic-bite-reset-type, walleye-pmic-wdt-readback-image, subject deep-sleep): proved on a charger-less kernel first, then armed in every charger-probing image. Until z10 reads the type, treat a bite as a power-off (z9). NOT KNOWN YET: whether TZ or the PMIC stalls; whether the kernel still answers on the bus (a root read of the usbfs control endpoint on the host, with the author's go, would tell); what the PON reason registers say after the power cycle (readable only from a kernel with the pon node bound - the z9/z10 line).

brief: The c3 'hang' is unproven: one witness (lsusb) kept a stale gadget while Android may have been up
question: Did the Pixel 2 hang in c3 for 44 minutes, or did the host keep a stale enumeration of our gadget?
found: Correction of lab research walleye-c3-hang-why (PR 250) and of the keeper's 'hung' call (PR 246). Facts from the host journal and sysfs: the c3 gadget (dev 65, serial walleye-first-boot) enumerated at 15:13:50 (local) and stayed on the bus until 15:57:09; Android (18d1:4ee7, dev 66, adb 'device product:lineage_walleye') enumerated at 15:57:12, 3 s later; the author says he did not reboot it and saw LineageOS on the screen throughout. Three seconds is far too short for a boot into Android, so either the phone had been in Android for some time with the host keeping a stale enumeration of our gadget (a USB host only drops a device when it sees the disconnect; a device that stops answering without releasing its pull-up stays listed), or the phone restarted much earlier and Android sat in a state the host did not list until something (a touch, a mode change of the USB configuration) made it re-enumerate. The record 'c3 never left the bus for 28+ min, so the SoC never reset' is therefore NOT PROVEN: it rests on lsusb alone, one witness. What the lane knows: the gadget stayed listed 44 minutes; adb never listed the phone in that time; the author saw Android on the screen (a command-mode panel also keeps its last frame, so the screen alone proves nothing either); the phone is in Android now. What the lane does not know: when the phone left c3 and whether the reset worked at 180 s as c2's did. The restart gate (decision 2026-11-18-walleye-restart-gate-before-charger-try) stays as a cheap check but its premise 'c3 hangs the phone' is withdrawn until the gate itself (restart-check.sh reading adb, fastboot and the tty beat, not lsusb alone) measures it. Also: 18d1:d001 'Nexus 4 (fastboot)' on bus 3 port 3-1 is NOT unknown: sysfs says product 'Qualcomm SM7150 Device', serial postmarketOS - it is surya's gadget (the other lab phone, on its own lease), listed under the generic vendor id's name.

brief: Pixel 2 UFS is Hynix 64GB, the maker Sony's quirks single out; mechanism of the yoshino erase unpublished; no way back if the bootloader goes; z11 needs the author's word
question: Can probing the Pixel 2's UFS damage the bootloader (the Sony yoshino failure)?
found: Android says 64GB Hynix (model/fw unreadable without root). Sony yoshino: probe without quirks erased the bootloader; the downstream fix is NO_PURGE (two Hynix models, one Samsung), EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH (all Hynix), AVAILTXDATALANES=1; nobody published why. Our 7.3 tree applies only HOST_PA_SAVECONFIGTIME and DELAY_BEFORE_LPM for Hynix; nothing in the driver sends purge by itself (only ufs_bsg), the probe sends reset, link startup, NOP, fDeviceInit, descriptor reads, power-mode change, SCSI scan. Chance: not zero, unknown; not measured.

brief: z12 built: z11 with only the kernel changed (Hynix UFS quirks); sha256 f959c448; not tried; review found the purge guard misses ufs_bsg
question: Can our 7.3 kernel carry Sony's Hynix UFS quirks, in a z11-identical image?
found: Kernel topic/ufs-hynix-quirks 12dca401a on e123d3bff: NO_PURGE, EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH (G1-3 = 0x48), ONE_TX_LANE on SKHYNIX ANY_MODEL in ufs_qcom_dev_fixups. z12 = z11 with only Image.gz changed (build-z12.sh, checks ok); images-z12/boot-z12.img sha256 f959c44868200c9a4056e5f6ffa56679e42b24a98f64f8337c87b8f791c74f41; never run. question: Is there a known way back from an erased bootloader on the Pixel 2 (EDL, test points, recovery)?
found: EDL 9008 is reached by Pixel 2s with a broken chain (several reports, Sahara HWID 0x0005e0e1, PK hash 7489217...), but recovery needs a firehose programmer signed to that hash; bkerler (2021): none released or leaked for Pixels; ~200-loader survey lists none; threads 2018-2025 end without a fix; Google's repair tool is Pixel 3+; no public test points for walleye. Verdict: no known way back, fairly sure. Preparable at no risk: read-back of xbl_a/b (4,149,248 B each, boot LUNs) and the rest of the boot chain as mode-600 files with sha256.

brief: z9's recovery after the PMIC bite is unproven as 'by itself' (the author's hold is a confound)
question: Did the phone come back by itself after the z9 PMIC bite?
found: Two rows of the lab say different things about the phone after the z9 PMIC bite: the z9 row says it did not come back by itself; the c3 try row (walleye-c3-tried) says z9 came back after about 10 minutes. The facts: after the z9 bite (14:54 local) the phone was off the USB bus; the keeper (session 348f6c2b) reported later that fastboot (18d1:4ee0, slot b current, successful) appeared 'a few minutes' after its last message, '>10 min', while the author held Power about 15 s in that same window (the coordinator's relay, 14:08-14:11Z, then Android 18d1:4ee7 with adb). The record does not tell which of the two recovered the phone. So the right wording for both rows: the recovery after a PMIC bite is UNPROVEN as 'by itself'; it is known only that the phone reappeared within about 15 minutes with the author's hold in the window. This research row corrects the c3 wording: wherever a row says 'z9 recovered by itself after 10 minutes', read: not proven (the hold is a confound).

brief: z15 once from slot b: gadget/telnet up at 18 s, but no RMI4 touch device: i2c@c179000 has compatible qcom,i2c-msm-v2 (downstream), so no mainline driver binds
question: Does the RMI4 controller probe on z15 (part 1, no touch)?
found: z15 booted once from slot b via lpoco lab fastboot boot; walleye-gadget-up passes (ping+telnet). Absent: no rmi4/synaptics dmesg line, /sys/class/input has only pm8941_pwrkey and gpio_keys, /sys/bus/i2c/devices empty, no touch irq. rmi4_i2c driver is registered (RMI4_CORE/I2C/F12 =y, I2C_QUP=y). brief: z16 built: z15 with the QUP i2c node renamed qup@c179000 so the vendor overlay no longer overwrites its compatible; sha256 05849ba7; 26 checks ok, rebuild identical
question: How does z16 get the mainline i2c-qup driver onto the touch controller's bus?
found: z15's dtb already had compatible qcom,i2c-qup-v2.2.1 at 0xc179000; the bootloader's overlay (dtbo entry 3, fragment@142) merges its own i2c@c179000 by name into it and overwrites compatible (qcom,i2c-msm-v2), clocks, clock-names, interrupts, dmas and pinctrl (fdtoverlay on z15: merged compatible qcom,i2c-msm-v2). So changing the compatible in our dtb, as the backlog item said, would have changed nothing on the phone. z16 = z15 with the node name i2c -> qup (same length; node plus the two /__symbols__ paths blsp1_i2c5 and rmi4_f12; 9 bytes differ); the overlay then adds its own driverless i2c@c179000 beside ours, and fragment@143 lands on the vendor stub i2c_5, so touchscreen@20 stays under ours. Proof: tests/host/i2c-qup-after-merge.sh fails on z15's dtb, passes on z16's (after fdtoverlay with dtbo entry 3); build/build-z16.sh 26 checks ok, rebuild identical; boot-z16.img sha256 05849ba71282898c3fc5c77c7fa4b34ffdf64504ea1014edfd809f020c358aaa, dtb fed46c5b12110838e88c7499613d12b4f622d3cab8172955407abd4c75dc6f8f; not tried on the phone.

brief: z16 once from slot b: i2c bus 0 and rmi4_i2c at 0-0020 appear, but probe fails -5 (set page select failed): the controller does not answer
question: Does the RMI4 controller probe on z16 (part 1, nobody touching)?
found: z16 booted once from slot b via lpoco lab fastboot boot; gadget-up passes (gadget at 18 s). Progress over z15: i2c bus i2c-0 (c179000.qup) and device 0-0020 now exist; i2c_qup irq 70 registered; rmi4_i2c bound and ran. dmesg: 'rmi_set_page: set page failed: -5', 'Failed to set page select to 0', 'probe with driver rmi4_i2c failed with error -5' (1.09 s). So no input device from touch (only event0/1, pwrkey and gpio keys). -EIO on first read means the bus works but the chip is silent: likely unpowered or held in reset (supply regulators for the touch vdd/vio, reset gpio89, or a needed delay) - the dtb's touchscreen@20 properties not yet checked against the vendor tree. Proof of walleye-try-z16-part1 not met (rmi4 lines yes, 'no failures' no). Phone returned to Android on slot b, stock kernel, nothing flashed, slots a and b successful, fastboot reachable. Material ~/lab-material/walleye/z16-part1 (dmesg.txt, probe.txt).

brief: Android resets the card's RST_n and runs it with one quirk and 2 lanes; z13 never resets it and adds 4 Hynix flags (1 TX lane): not a match; abl hand-over and HW version unread
question: How does Android bring up this exact UFS card (vendor GPL kernel + live), and does our z13 path match it? Is a probe safe enough to take back to the author?
found:
Read: Google kernel/msm android-msm-wahoo-4.4-android11 @52750b8f (the phone runs a LineageOS 4.4.302 fork, its UFS files not read), the keeper's live readings, ours at d49d54405 (z13). Compared with scripts (PHY tables as sorted lists, quirk tables, dts props live fdt vs our dtb) and by hand (reset, power-up, link startup, power mode). Rerun: material scripts/run-all.sh.
Android: host full reset, then a hardware RST_n pulse on the card (pinctrl ufs_reset low/high 10-15 us), then HCE: PHY reset 1 ms, tables, release, serdes start, PCS ready; link startup (G1 slow-auto, RX linecfg on, core clk 150, hw clock gating, LCC 0, REG1 mask); for THIS card (H28U74301AMR) only the quirk HOST_PA_SAVECONFIGTIME applies (vendor Hynix model entries are prefixes hB8aL1.. and do not match); HS-G3, rate B, 2 lanes each way; purge never sent (live: only fDeviceInit set).
Ours differs: (1) no card reset at all: no reset-gpios, and pinctrl-msm8998 ngpios=150 while UFS_RESET is pin 153, so it cannot be described; (2) z13 adds DELAY_BEFORE_LPM, EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH, NO_PURGE (guard), ONE_TX_LANE: Sony's workarounds for other cards (hB8aL1/hC8aL1 D001) that Android proves this card does not need; one TX lane is a link Android never ran; (3) PHY: mainline msm8998 uses the sdm845 tables; vs vendor 3.1.0 table 10 differing lines (PLL_IVCO 0x0f vs 0x07, RX_EQU_ADAPTOR_CNTRL4 0x1d vs 0x1b, ours-only TX_RES_CODE_LANE_OFFSET and RX_MODE_00), vs 3.0.0 35 lines; which table Android ran is not known yet (HW version register unread); (4) no ICE, no phy/pll loads, plain clocks instead of hw_ctl ones, no bus votes/pm-qos, extra caps (clk scaling, WB, rpm autosuspend).
Sony's three fixes appear nowhere in the vendor sequence for this card; the erase mechanism stays unpublished, so nothing shows our path safe.
Verdict: z13 does not match Android and its extra Hynix flags move it away. Matching = SAVECONFIGTIME only (keep the NO_PURGE guard), the right PHY table, ICE/loads, and a card RST_n pulse (needs a kernel change: widen tlmm gpios or pinctrl states). Even matched, the probe is not safe enough to take to the author: abl's hand-over state is unread, the erase cause unknown, no way back (EDL). Provable before any try without our UFS: on live Android with root read UFS_HW_VERSION (0xe0), the full host regs and the PHY regs, and the ufs_reset pad state. Not known yet: abl hand-over, HW version, Lineage-fork differences.

brief: z17 read-only: the pmi8998 gpio chip exists (gpiochip2, 14 GPIOs, phandle matches) yet regulator-touch-power says 'can't get GPIO'
question: Why is the pmi8998 gpio chip absent on z17?
found:
z17 once from slot b (fastboot boot now; gadget 1d6b:0104 at 18 s), read only over the network shell (telnet 172.16.43.1). Nothing written but debugfs mount.
Facts: the pmi8998 gpio chip EXISTS: gpiochip2 = 800f000.spmi:pmic@2:gpio@c000, 14 GPIOs (gpiochip1 = pm8998 pmic@0, 26 GPIOs; gpiochip0 = tlmm 150). spmi devices 0-00..0-03 all bound to pmic-spmi. dmesg: 'qcom,pm8998@0' and 'qcom,pmi8998@3' nodes 'err -22 does not have reg' (stray vendor-style nodes; the real nodes are pmic@N). The touch regulator's gpios = <0x60 2 0>, and phandle 0x60 is pmi8998_gpios (pmic@2 gpio@c000), i.e. the existing chip. Yet devices_deferred says 'regulator-touch-power  reg-fixed-voltage: can't get GPIO' and 'i2c 0-0020: supplier regulator-touch-power not ready'. pmic@2 gpio2 reads in/low/normal (not driven). regulators: l6, l28 disabled; touch-power not registered.
So the premise 'chip absent because pmi8998@3 lacks reg' is wrong (confirms builder's falsified premise). New question: why does gpiod_get fail for a chip that exists - probe order (regulator-fixed probed before gpiochip2 and not retried?), or gpio-ranges/pinctrl-less gpiochip lookup, or line 2 not requestable. dmesg for the gpio probe time was not captured (filter lacked timestamps of pmic@2 gpio probe); next read: full dmesg and 'cat /sys/kernel/debug/gpio' after force re-probe is NOT done (would write).

brief: Touch power gpio: our specifier is valid; the failure is a persistent -EPROBE_DEFER at one of two leaves (no gpio device matched, or no pinctrl range), not settled by source alone
question: Exactly why does gpiod_get of regulator-touch-power fail although the pmi8998 gpiochip2 (14 GPIOs) exists?
found: Read from v7.3 source and the built z17 dtb. (1) The specifier is right: dtb gpios <0x60 2 0>; 0x60 = pmic@2/gpio@c000, compatible qcom,pmi8998-gpio, #gpio-cells 2, gpio-ranges <0x60 0 0 14>; pmic_gpio_of_xlate returns 2-1 = offset 1 (PMIC_GPIO_PHYSICAL_OFFSET 1), below 14; debugfs shows gpiochip2 gpio2 as a normal line. Host proof: tests/host/touch-gpio-specifier.sh passes. So no 1-based/label/ngpios error (the driver table says 14 for pmi8998). (2) The failure is -EPROBE_DEFER (-517): devices_deferred lists only deferred probes; the string is fixed.c's dev_err_probe after gpiod_get_optional; dd.c clears the reason at every retry, so it is the last retry's, which came after pmic@2's gpio probe (late_initcall retry and every later bind): not a mere ordering race. (3) Non-defer errnos (-EINVAL from xlate, -EBUSY, pinmux errors) would not be listed: ruled out. (4) Source leaves that return -EPROBE_DEFER with the chip present: (a) of_find_gpio_device_by_xlate finds no gpio_device (its of_node is not the specifier's node, or xlate fails); (b) pinctrl_get_device_gpio_range finds no range for the line and pinctrl_ready_for_gpio_range is false (gpiochip_generic_request); (c) try_module_get on the owner: impossible, PINCTRL_QCOM_SPMI_PMIC=y. Mainline sdm845 users of the same pmi8998 dtsi work, so the source gives no static reason; which of (a)/(b) is not known yet. (5) No pin config is needed first: the line is muxed by the request itself; the overlay's switch-gpio (tlmm 75) is another pin and not on this path. (6) Our kernel has CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG off, so the gpio core's dev_dbg lines ('cannot find GPIO chip', 'gpiod_request: status -517') never print: why the z17 dmesg names no leaf. Cheapest settle: read-only z-next reads (per-pinctrl gpio-ranges in debugfs, gpiochip2 of_node vs the regulator's phandle) and a diagnostic kernel with dynamic debug and dyndbg on the command line.

brief: z20 built: z19 with a diagnostic kernel (dynamic debug, DEBUG_GPIO) and dyndbg for gpiolib, gpiolib-of, pinctrl core and devicetree on the command line; sha256 fe9e0cce; rebuild identical
question: Can one boot print which gpio/pinctrl leaf the touch power gpio defers at, and the errno?
found: The kernel is z15's tree (linux-phone-oco/linux topic/pmic-wdt-wake-in-suspend e123d3bff) built with build/walleye.config plus build/walleye-diag.config (CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG=y, CONFIG_DEBUG_GPIO=y; build-kernel.sh takes EXTRA_CONFIG). brief: Touch, Android vs z20: Android's synaptics node (i2c, power-gpio pmi8998 gpio 2, reset tlmm 89, irq 125) is absent in ours; pmi gpio 2 is out-high on Android, in-low on ours
question: What does live Android set for touch that our kernel does not?
found: Captured with part-compare.sh (touch list) on live Android (adb root) and on z20 (fe9e0cce, network shell, one try from slot b, fell back to Android b by itself at 180 s; nothing flashed). Material ~/lab-material/walleye/compare-touch-{android-20261119-004949,ours-20261119-005129,diff.txt}, never in git. Findings: (1) Android's i2c bus carries a synaptics_dsx@20 child (irq-gpio tlmm 125, reset-gpio tlmm 89, switch-gpio tlmm 75, power-gpio pmi8998 gpio 2 with power-on-state 1, reset delay 20 ms, two pinctrl states active/suspend); input device synaptics_dsxv26 is up. Ours has no such child and no touch input device (only pwrkey, gpio-keys). (2) Pad state of the power line: Android, the pmi8998 gpio claimed by the touch driver reads out/high; ours pmi8998 gpio2 reads in/low, pull-down (no owner). (3) i2c bus pinctrl differs only in phandle numbers; its gpios (87/88) agree. (4) Regulator and clk diffs are the whole-SoC list, not touch specific; no touch regulator is enabled first on Android (tps61099-vbus disabled on both). Reading: the missing pieces are the node itself and the shared pmi8998 gpio 2 owner (z20's proxy never registers), consistent with research walleye-z20-tried-touch-gpio-leaf. Next: build item walleye-touch-gpio-shared-proxy, then add the synaptics node with these gpios. Phone left on Android slot b; fastboot flags a and b successful.

brief: Second claimant of pmi8998 gpio 2 found (overlay synaptics_dsx@20 under stub i2c_5); fix = /vendor-overlay-stubs disabled; a UFS-on z21 was built and is NOT to boot
question: Who else claims pmi8998 gpio 2 so that gpiolib_shared.proxy.0 is needed, and can our dtb stop it without touching the phone's own overlay?
found: After the stock dtbo overlay (entry 3) merges, two nodes name the gpio by a gpio property: our /regulator-touch-power and the overlay's synaptics_dsx@20 (synaptics,power-gpio <pmi8998 gpio 2>), which the overlay puts under the label i2c_5 - an empty stub of ours inside /vendor-overlay-stubs. drivers/gpio/gpiolib-shared.c (gpio_shared_of_traverse) skips a node whose status is not okay together with its children, and makes a gpio shared when two nodes name it; the proxy never registered on z20. The overlay cannot be edited, but its place can: status = disabled on /vendor-overlay-stubs (build/gen-overlay-stubs.sh and the dtsi, landed). tests/host/touch-gpio-single-claimant.sh merges the overlay and counts available claimants: z19/z20 dtb 2 (fail, seen first), with the change 1 (pass). build/build-z21.sh repacks z20 with that one dtb change (all checks ok, rebuild identical, sha256 58994599) - but z20 has UFS on, so that image is moved to NOT-TO-BOOT-ufs-on-images-z21 and never queued. brief: UFS was enabled in every image since z11 and probed at least four times against the author's 'Yes, wait'; the card and the bootloader survived
question: Did our images probe the UFS card after the author's 'Yes, wait', and what happened to the card?
found: Found 2026-11-19 by the upstreams inventory, confirmed read-only: our shared dts (dt/msm8998-google-walleye.dts) has had &ufshc and &ufsphy status = "okay" since the z11 commit (lab PR 274, 'ufs readonly z11'); every image built from main after that carries the UFS host enabled, with the UFS driver built into the kernel. The author's answer 'Yes, wait' (decision 2026-11-18-walleye-ufs-wait) was meant to keep z11 and z13 unrun, and the lane held those two tries: but the same dts line enabled UFS in the later images, which the lane did try (z14, z15, z16, z17, z19?, z20 and the shell captures): the captured dmesgs of z15, z16, z17 and z20 (lab-material z15-part1, z16-part1, z17-part1, z20-try1) show 'scsi host0: ufshcd', the SKhynix H28U74301AMR D003 enumerated (well-known LUN), and for z15/z16/z17 the other LUNs attached as sda..sdf with the partition scans ('Attached SCSI disk' lines): i.e. our kernel brought the link up and READ the card at least four times, unattended, on stock v7.3 quirks only (no z13 backport in those images: z15+ came from the touch lane's kernel; check the exact config per image), against the author's wait. Nothing was written to the card by us (no mount, read-only init), the phone still boots Android from both slots (adb device, a/b successful) and the bootloader is intact: that is REAL EVIDENCE for the risk question (the yoshino erase did not happen on this card with the plain probe: at least 4 captured probes, probably more uncaptured), and not a licence: it does not show the quirk-less probe is safe in every sequence (the erase cause is unpublished). How it happened: the ufs-readonly build item put the enable into the shared dts instead of a z11-only dts, and no check said 'UFS stays off until the author says go'; the keepers booted images by the try items, not by what their dtb enables. The author's 'Yes, wait' is withdrawn from the keepers' hands now: UFS off in every image, a host gate, and the author told plainly. ADDENDUM 2026-11-19 (item walleye-ufs-off-gate; tests/host/ufs-off-inventory.sh over ~/Projects/walleye-build/images*/boot-*.img, 97 images, z21 included): 58 are NOT TO BOOT, each marked by a NOT-TO-BOOT-IMAGE.txt beside it: 49 have UFS on, 9 (images/boot-a..i, built before the dtb carried symbols) cannot be shown off because the phone's overlay does not merge into their dtb. By images directory: images-pk456: pk5 pk6; images-z20: z20; images-z11: z11; images-vfx: vfa vfb vfc vfd; images-z12: z12; images-w: w1 w2 w3 w4 w5 wa wr; images-pk5l: pk5l; images-z13: z13; images-x: x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x7; images: a b c d e f g h i; images-pk5l2: pk5l2; images-z15: z15; images-z16: z16; images-z17: z17; images-vf1: vf1; images-z19: z19; images-vf2: vf2; images-vf3: vf3; images-t1: t1; images-pk2: pk1 pk2; images-wp: wp1 wp2 wp3 wp4 wp5 wpa; images-vf4: vf4; images-nocon: pk3; images-t3: t3; images-pk: pk1 pk2; images-g: g1 g2 g3;  The stock-kernel vendor images (vf1-vf4, vfa-vfd) are on through the vendor dtb merged with the phone's own overlay; every other UFS-on one carries a mainline-style dtb (/soc@0/ufshc@1da4000) with status okay, from z11's shared dts on. 39 are off, among them the new z21. After this: dt/msm8998-google-walleye.dts has &ufshc and &ufsphy disabled, the z11-z13 experiments take dt/msm8998-google-walleye-ufs.dts, and tests/host/ufs-off-image.sh gates every build script that writes a boot image (a stock-kernel repack fails it by design until it has a UFS-off dtb).
