brief: Gear 1 at idle is most likely clock-scale-down (legacy path, no OPP table), not a missed G3: the link is already HS rate B, so the power-mode change was made
question: Why does the link idle at HS gear 1 and the change to HS-G3 is not seen: clock scaling at idle, the power-mode change not made, or the PHY table?
found: From try 1 files (link.txt: dev_pm=SLEEP gear=HS_GEAR1 lane=2 mode=FAST_MODE rate=HS_RATE_B state=HIBERN8; dmesg: PHY table 3.1.0, no UFS error, six LUNs read by 1.64 s) and v7.3 source (wt-k-ufsm). EXCLUDED by the files: 'power-mode change not made'. ufshcd_init_pwr_info leaves PWM G1, 1 lane, SLOWAUTO, hs_rate 0; the try shows FAST_MODE, rate B, 2 lanes, so ufshcd_config_pwr_mode ran and reached HS on both lanes; lane 1 and the PHY table (3.1.0 loaded, link up, partition tables read) are not what holds it. RANKED: (1) clock scale-down at idle, most likely: ufs-qcom sets CAP_CLK_SCALING, msm8998.dtsi has freq-table-hz (50/200 MHz core, 37.5/150 MHz unipro) and no operating-points table, so hba->use_pm_opp is false and ufs_qcom_freq_to_gear_speed returns UFS_HS_DONT_CHANGE (0); ufshcd_scale_gear then takes the legacy path and drops the gear to clk_scaling.min_gear = G1 when devfreq (polling 60 ms, down below load threshold) scales down after the boot-time partition reads; the sysfs gear is hba->pwr_info, which holds the scaled-down value; 170 s idle is long enough. (2) Gear capped below G3 by the host side: ufs_qcom_get_hs_gear returns G3 for host major <4 (3.1.0 here), so no mainline cap; a DT limit would show only if the board file sets a limit property (none seen in the match overlay): unlikely. (3) PHY table 3.1.0 against the vendor's: would show as link or read errors, not a quiet G1; unlikely, and G3 never attempted so also not proven. (4) Reading at hibern8 with dev_pm=SLEEP is only the sampling state, not a fault. Not yet known: clkscale_enable and devfreq state, power_info after a bounded read load, whether a scale-up to G3 happens under load. READ-ONLY readings for try 2: cat clkscale_enable and the devfreq node (cur_freq, available_frequencies, governor) of 1da4000.ufshc; power_info right after dd of the first MiB of sda (O_DIRECT, read only) and again after 2 s idle; a count of ufshcd power-mode / scale lines in dmesg with dyndbg on drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c (+p) for the try. If gear reaches 3 under load and falls back at idle: works, as Android does; if it never leaves 1 under load: look at devfreq and a missing opp (a DT operating-points-v2 table with the 150/37.5 MHz pairs mapped to gear in ufs_qcom_freq_to_gear_speed would then be the fix, an upstream-able DT change).

brief: A bite with USB in boots charger mode because the S2 reset type 7 (hard) power-cycles the PMIC and USB then counts as the power-on reason; the S2 type the firmware left (1, warm) is the one to try
question: Why does a PMIC-watchdog bite with USB in boot the bootloader's charger screen, and should the PON or the reset type make it warm-boot?
found: READ, not measured on the bite: (1) Qualcomm: the PMIC records WHY it powered on in PON_REASON1 (KPDPWR_N, CBLPWR_N cable, USB_CHG, DC_CHG, hard-reset bit) and PON_ON_REASON separates a warm reset (0x40) from a normal power-on (0x80); the vendor says WARM_RESET is for crash dumps, HARD_RESET for restarting the device. (2) Our driver writes S2 type 0x07 (hard): the PMIC then powers its rails down and up like a cold start, so with the cable in the power-on reason is the cable (USB_CHG/CBLPWR_N), not a key press or a warm reset. A bootloader that sees a charger reason and no key press shows its off-mode charging screen: that matches the author's words (charging icon, black screen, Android only after a short power press). (3) The firmware had left S2 at type 0x01 (warm), read by the driver at probe ('S2 reset control was 0x1', booted 2026-11-20 run); mainline's own constants are 0x01 warm, 0x04 shutdown, 0x07 hard. A warm type keeps the PMIC peripherals on and sets the warm-reset bit, which bootloaders of this family read as 'not a cold boot' and do not send to the charger screen (the Qualcomm LK rule, recalled, NOT read: walleye's bootloader is closed and its rule is not confirmed here). (4) Android reported boot reason [reboot] after the later power press: that is Android's reading of the second boot, and says nothing of the bite's reason. NOT KNOWN YET: the PON_REASON/POFF/ON_REASON registers right after the bite (nobody read them before the second boot: the run read them only before arming); why z9 without patch 1 powered off while the firmware type was 1 (maybe the type was never read back there); what stock Android's own watchdog bite does on this phone (stock reset type). OPTIONS: A) arm S2 with warm type 0x01 (the firmware's own): smallest change, the series already has the reset-type hook; risk: the earlier z9 power-off; B) keep hard 0x07 and accept the charger screen when USB is in (the phone does restart; user-visible only with a cable); C) a PON bit or boot-reason handover before the bite (PON_SOFT_RB_SPARE as qcom-pon.c uses for reboot modes): works only if the bootloader reads it, unproven; D) leave it to the user space: nothing. LEAN: A, tried first because it is the firmware's own value, read-only experiment first (item walleye-wdt-bite-pon-reasons-read). Does not block the series: the bite proof stands.

brief: Splash image B-s5 built, never booted: B-d5 plus a no-map reservation at 0x9d400000 and a simple-framebuffer (8 MDSS clocks, MDSS_GDSC) in its dtb; 17 checks ok, rebuild identical
question: Can the splash handover be fixed in the dts, as decision 2026-11-19-walleye-display-flip-dts-not-timing says, and built as an image to try at 5 s?
found: dt/msm8998-google-walleye-display-splash.dts is the source (values of mainline's OnePlus 5/5T common file and the GPL wahoo dts: 0x9d400000, 0x2400000, 1080x1920 a8r8g8b8). Today's board file does not compile in the display kernel's tree (no fuel-gauge labels), so build/build-display-splash-image.sh makes the same change on B-d5's own dtb, as L4 was made from L3: no line removed, two nodes, three /chosen properties and two symbols added. tests/host/dtb-display-splash.sh fails on B-d5's dtb and passes on the new one; the region overlaps no other reserved one. Kernel, ramdisk (init-display-delay, 5 s), header, cmdline and size are B-d5's; AVB, UFS-off gate, overlay merge, touch and panel gpio claimants pass; rebuilt identical. images-display-splash/boot-b-s5.img sha256 b7c827e9a3f55a7ee6e68752430a19bdad2de3262bc22a5cc0379cd3df80df58. Not tried: whether the faults, rcg warning and DSI -110 vanish at 5 s is the keeper's bisect.

brief: B-s5 (splash reserved, simple-framebuffer) at 5 s: all three signs stay, same as B-d5: SMMU faults 10, rcg warnings 4, DSI -110 5; 13 of 13 modules ok
question: With the splash region reserved and a simple-framebuffer in the dtb, do the SMMU faults, the pclk0 rcg warning and the DSI -110 vanish at a 5 s load?
found: One unattended RAM boot of B-s5 (nothing flashed) by procedures/display-delay-bisect-on-the-pixel-2.rs with delays=5, image_prefix=b-s (device.toml put back after): sha, UFS-off and battery checks ok, 11 steps passed, phone back on Android slot b. Against B-d5 (SMMU 10, rcg 4, -110 5) and B-d25 (all 0): SMMU faults did NOT vanish (10 level-2 context faults, cb 0, iova 0x9d4e1400..0x9d56c000, inside the now-reserved 0x9d400000 region, at 6.19 s); pclk0/byte0 rcg warnings did NOT vanish (4, at 6.22-6.24 s); DSI -110 did NOT vanish (EXIT_SLEEP_MODE and Failed to initialize panel at 6.48 s, the first 0x51 backlog write -110 at 6.69 s, drm_panel_enable failed to enable backlight); fb0 msmdrmfb still registers at 8.57 s. So reserving the region and describing it as simple-framebuffer does not stop the scanout from faulting through msm's new SMMU domain nor the bootloader's DSI clocks from being re-programmed; a simple-framebuffer alone does not hand the splash over. No simple-framebuffer line in the kernel log (grep simple-fb/simplefb: none): whether it bound is not known yet. Table and dmesg kept in ~/lab-material/walleye/display-delay-b-s-20261120-011649/. Next: read whether simple-framebuffer probed (its clocks/GDSC held), then the handover in the driver (disable scanout / stop DSI clocks before msm attaches) or load after 25 s.

brief: The faults are msm's new SMMU domain meeting a live scan-out; no board hands over cleanly (OnePlus 5, Pixel 3 skip msm); cheapest try: reset MDSS_BCR at mdss probe
question: Why did the reserved splash not stop the SMMU faults at 6 s, and how do other msm platforms hand the bootloader's scan-out over?
found: (1) Our mmss_smmu (qcom,msm8998-smmu-v2) takes qcom_smmu_cfg_probe: the bootloader's valid SMRs are kept as BYPASS across the SMMU reset. That holds only until a device attaches a translating domain. 'preserved 0 boot mappings' in our log is the ACPI IORT RMR path and means nothing on DT. (2) msm_iommu_new does iommu_paging_domain_alloc + iommu_attach_device: the S2CR of mdss SID 0 moves to a new empty context bank, and the scan-out, still reading physical 0x9d4xxxxx, faults (SID 0x0, cb 0); first fault 5 ms after dpu_kms_hw_init. iommu-addresses direct mappings are applied by the IOMMU core to default domains only (iommu.c ~671, 3186, 3221), so msm's own domain does not get them: the walleye coordinator's lead (2) is right as far as it goes, but its mapping would not reach msm. iommu.passthrough=1 does not help either (msm allocates its own paging domain). No mainline commit found that stops the scan-out before the attach (not proof none exists). (3) B-s5's simple-framebuffer cannot have bound: no SIMPLEDRM, SYSFB_SIMPLEFB or FB_SIMPLE in arm64 defconfig or our fragments; its clocks were never held. The cmdline has clk_ignore_unused ('Not disabling unused clocks' in the log), so clk_disable_unused is not what stops the scan-out near 25 s; the earlier read (no kernel event 12-25 s) points at the bootloader side; genpd and regulator late-off timers are also ruled out for the 16-26 s window (regulators at 30 s; genpd at init, and pd is held by clk/pd state). Not known yet: what stops it. (4) Others: OnePlus 5/5T reserve cont_splash_mem and describe a simplefb but never enable mdss; Pixel 3 crosshatch disables mdss and dispcc 'so simple-framebuffer continues working'; OnePlus 6 enables mdss beside simplefb (fault-free not verified); Fxtec Pro1 reserves only. No board found loads msm over a live splash and says it is clean. The 2019 Andersson/Hugo RFC saw exactly our failure and was not merged. (5) The DSI -110 and pclk0 rcg warnings (DSI/PLL re-programmed under a live bootloader state) are what break the panel, more than the faults, which Hugo calls non-fatal. (6) msm_mdss_reset (assert, 20 ms, deassert) exists but the msm8998 mdss node has no resets property; MDSS_BCR (mmcc 0x2300) is registered and mdss-common.yaml has resets: a dts-only line would make mdss probe reset the whole MDSS block (scan-out, DSI host, pingpong) before msm attaches. Ranked hypotheses: A the bootloader's scan-out and DSI state are live and only a reset or quiesce before attach helps (try: resets = <&mmcc MDSS_BCR>); B the stop at 25 s is something outside the kernel that a read of the DPU registers at 5 s and 30 s will show; C pre-map the region in msm's domain (silences faults, leaves DSI -110: a part, not the way); D disable mdss until late like crosshatch (works, is the delay in the dts); E identity-attach msm (loses isolation, upstream-unfriendly). Material: researcher's survey, kept as this row only.

brief: After a bite the PON reasons can be read only where the phone first answers; a power press is a power-on that rewrites PON_REASON1, so POFF/WARM_RESET are the ones that can outlive it (not measured)
question: How can the PON registers be read after a PMIC watchdog bite on this phone, before anything resets them: the bootloader's charger screen has no adb, and Android's dmesg after the power press is already a second boot?
found: READ in this session: the driver's own constants (drivers/watchdog/pm8916_wdt.c): POFF_REASON1 is 0x0c (first generation) and 0xc5 (second generation, PM8998), PMIC_WD is its bit 2; the S2 type is the low nibble of 0x56, S2 enable is bit 7 of 0x57; the ramdisk of image A already reads those through the regmap debugfs (pon-regs). RECALLED from the downstream qpnp-power-on driver, NOT re-read: PON_REASON1 at 0x08, WARM_RESET_REASON1 at 0x0a; the offset of PON_ON_REASON on PM8998 is NOT confirmed, so the procedure reads 0x08..0x0d and 0xc0..0xc7 raw and names only 0x08, 0x0a, 0x0c and 0xc5. WHAT READS WHERE: (1) Android by itself (a warm bite may bring it back without a hand): adb gives ro.boot.bootreason and, if adb may read the kernel log, the PMIC's own reason lines; raw registers need root. (2) The bootloader by itself (fastboot lists the phone): our image booted again from memory reads the reason blocks; fastboot boot is a jump, not a PMIC reset (recalled, not measured). (3) The charger screen or an off phone: nothing answers (no adb, no fastboot), so a reading needs a hand: a power press or power+volume down; either is a power-on from off, which rewrites PON_REASON1 with the key: so for a cable-in hard bite PON_REASON1 cannot show the bite, and only the registers that outlive a power-on (POFF_REASON1 and WARM_RESET_REASON1, recalled to persist until the next power-off or warm reset, NOT measured) can. NOT KNOWN YET: which of these holds on this phone, and the PON_ON_REASON offset: the procedure saves every register raw with the path that read it (Android, our image), so the four bites decide it. DECIDED FROM THIS: the lab reads at the first place the phone answers without a hand; it asks the author only for the physical acts of the paths above, and never before it has said what it could see by itself.

brief: Install stage: two stages (rootfs on the unused slot's system partition written from Android, kernel still from RAM; then boot flashed); ~8 build h + ~8 keeper h; no mainline UFS write needed
question: How far is Linux installed on the Pixel 2 and booting from its own storage, what does each step cost, what is its way back, and what must the author say yes to?
found:
WHAT IS (measured, from the lab's own files, nothing written to the phone). UFS LUN layout read back 2026-11-19 (~/lab-material/walleye/bootchain-2026-11-19-2): sda (59.4 GiB) holds BOTH slots' abl, tz, hyp, boot (32 MiB each, sda9 boot_a, sda30 boot_b), dtbo (8 MiB), vbmeta (64 KiB), system (2.5 GiB: system_a sda22, system_b sda43), vendor (500 MiB) and userdata sda45 (53.2 GiB, shared by both slots); xbl_a/b live in the boot LUNs sdb/sdc (4 MiB); persist, misc, frp, modemst in sdd; fsg in sdf; metadata in sde. The boot-chain read-back (32 partitions, abl, xbl, tz, hyp ... ddr, cdt, sha256, twice identical, mode 600, kept off git) is the restore source for those; it does NOT include boot, dtbo, vbmeta, misc, system, vendor of either slot: they are not backed up yet (the control boot.img and dtbo.img sit in ~/Projects/walleye-build/control). Bootloader (getvar all 2026-11-17): unlocked, avb 1.0.0 user-settable key, both slots successful, no fastbootd, max-download 512 MiB; it picks dtbo entry 3 (id 0x1bc rev 3) itself and merges it onto our dtb; the lane's logs say Android runs from slot b, the brief says boot_b with slot a Android: which slot Android sits on must be read (fastboot getvar current-slot) before any write; the rule is: write the slot Android is NOT on. UFS: the matched image read the card (version 3.1.0, six LUNs, partition tables, no errors); the link idles at HS gear 1, 2 lanes; nothing has been written to the card by us. Standing decisions: Android is throw-away, the one hard line is bricking (2026-11-18-walleye-android-disposable-no-bricking: a write to one slot's boot, dtbo or vbmeta with a read-back backup and the other slot intact is the lane's call); no known way back from an erased bootloader (2026-11-18-walleye-edl-no-way-back-wait-holds); the UFS go is the author's.
HOW OTHERS INSTALL. (1) postmarketOS on Pixel A/B phones (crosshatch MR 83): one slot only is flashed; pmbootstrap flasher flash_rootfs to the system partition, or --partition userdata when system is too small, then flash_kernel (boot) and fastboot reboot. (2) The Nura/pmOS wiki for the Pixel 2 XL (taimen, same MSM8998 and UFS family): mainline boots with basic dts and USB network gives a shell; clk_ignore_unused needed; its device package was never added, so no one ships a Pixel 2/XL install; its partition map has our shape (boot_a/b, system_a/b, vendor_a/b, userdata, dtbo, vbmeta). (3) Mobian/Debian on OnePlus 6 (sdm845): fastboot flash boot, fastboot erase userdata, flash userdata (sparse, -S 100M), fastboot erase dtbo, reboot: rootfs on userdata, dtbo erased so the bootloader takes our dtb. (4) OnePlus 5 (msm8998, nearest sibling): a ramdisk mounts a loopback rootfs.img from the userdata partition root; pmaports MR 3531 carries it installed to internal storage on mainline 6.0. (5) AVB: an unlocked bootloader boots an image whose hash does not match vbmeta (orange state, a warning screen); the usual extra step on Pixels is fastboot flash --disable-verity --disable-verification vbmeta, for system/vendor verity, which our kernel does not use. Nobody has published a Pixel 2 (walleye/taimen) rootfs on its own UFS with a mainline kernel; the sibling OnePlus 5 has.
KEY FINDING. Writing the rootfs does not need mainline to write UFS. Android already writes UFS (its own proven stack). So the install splits in stages that each have a way back: STAGE 1 'rootfs on its own storage': while Android runs from slot X, dd a rootfs image onto the OTHER slot's system partition (2.5 GiB, adb root, after reading it back with sha256); boot our kernel from RAM with fastboot boot as now, UFS on, initramfs mounts that partition read-only with a tmpfs overlay: no flash, no set_active, no bootloader-visible change, no mainline UFS write; the phone returns to Android by itself (reboot). That reaches docs step rootfs-boots (root on the storage, ssh over usb-network is the proof). STAGE 2 'boots by itself': read back boot_Y, dtbo_Y, vbmeta_Y, then fastboot flash boot_Y (our image, stock dtbo), set_active Y; boot counting (retry-count) and the power key fall back to the other slot. AVB and the slot rollback are unmeasured for this phone (not known yet): the first flash of boot_Y is the cheap measurement, its way back is the read-back file and the other slot. STAGE 3 mainline UFS WRITE (ext4 rw, a persistent system) is later and the only stage with the Sony-class hazard (purge/erase/unmap): mount nodiscard, no fstrim, the purge guard, and prove after every write run that the bootloader files read back with the same sha256 as the stored set (bootchain-readback-check, twice on the same bytes).
WHERE THE ROOTFS GOES. system_<other> 2.5 GiB (the first image: fits Alpine, pmOS-style, or minimal Debian with systemd and ssh, 0.5-0.8 GiB; a phone-UI image does not, Mobian-size images need userdata). userdata 53 GiB is shared by both slots, so using it ends Android's data and Android boots to setup (disposable by decision; way back = fastboot erase userdata plus Google's public factory image): keep for stage 3. A new partition or a GPT edit is rejected: the bootloader reads the GPT, mainline would write it, no way back known. A loopback rootfs.img in userdata (OnePlus 5 way) is an option later, not now.
THE DISTRO. Postponed by the author (Debian or Nura); the earlier decision rows were not found in this base by search. Costs HERE: Debian minimal: no tooling on this lab machine today (debootstrap, mmdebstrap, qemu-user-static, pmbootstrap are not installed; mkfs.ext4, img2simg, avbtool, fastboot are), so installing them is a yes; we own the initramfs and init (lpoco-bringup generic init, usb gadget already working), so ~3 agent-h to a bootable minimal image with ssh; systemd, glibc; ~0.5 GiB; nothing proprietary in it; firmware, modem and TAS2557 data stay out of git (read from the phone into ~/lab-material, as decided). Nura (pmOS, Alpine, OpenRC, musl): pmbootstrap builds the rootfs and its own initramfs but needs a device package (deviceinfo, our kernel as a package, the dtb, boot.img rules) nobody wrote for walleye or taimen: ~6-8 agent-h and pmbootstrap (chroots, qemu) installed; it brings phone-UI images, upstream packaging and a path to contribute back. Either way the rootfs sits in its own partition and is swappable: the first image does not bind the final distro. Recommendation: Debian minimal first (fewest new moving parts to reach ssh); the author picks the final distro before a phone-UI image.
THE WAY BACK. Stage 1: nothing to undo (the Android slot untouched, reboot returns); restore system_<other> by dd of the read-back file with its sha256 checked. Stage 2: fastboot flash boot_Y from the read-back file, set_active back; retry counter and power key fall back. Not undoable: the bootloader and xbl/abl partitions (never written by us), an erase of either, a purge: no EDL way exists (research 2026-11-18-walleye-edl-way-back); those steps are in no queue.
HONEST DISTANCE. Today Linux is not installed: every boot is from RAM, nothing on the card is ours. Stage 1 = rootfs-boots: UFS-root kernel+initramfs ~4 agent-h, Debian rootfs ~3 agent-h (+tooling yes), read-back ~1 keeper-h, write ~1 keeper-h, 2-3 boot tries ~3 keeper-h: about 7-8 build hours and 5 keeper hours, 2-3 working days of the lane if the display work does not take the keeper. Stage 2 (boots by itself): +3 keeper hours, +1 day. Stage 3 (writable system, gear 3): UFS try 2 (gear, OPP table) is already queued, a write test ~4 keeper-h; ~2 more days. Not known yet: avb behaviour on flash, whether UFS at gear 1 stays stable under load (the gear try is separate), which slot Android sits on, what Android does when userdata is gone. The display does not gate rootfs-boots (ssh over usb is the proof); display-reset-image only gives the installed system a screen.

brief: Google's wahoo tree (android11-release): stock system is slot-selected with avb, UFS host 1da4000.ufshc, recovery.wipe wipes system/vendor/userdata then boot; supports stage 1; Elixir repartitions
question: What do Google's own fstab.hardware and recovery files say about the stock partitions, mounts and A/B layout, for the install stage?
found:
Read 2026-11-20 from android.googlesource.com device/google/wahoo, branch android11-release (commit 5361539c, 2020-09-16; which Android build the phone runs is not known yet, so the match to the phone's build is not checked). Files that exist there: fstab.hardware, fstab.postinstall, init.recovery.hardware.rc, recovery.wipe, init.hardware.rc, init.insmod.sh and others; no proprietary-files lists.
fstab.hardware: (1) system mounts at / ext4 ro,barrier=1 with fs_mgr flags wait,slotselect,avb: the stock root is the SLOT-SELECTED system partition, checked by AVB, so stage 1's use of system_<other> follows the stock A/B scheme; our rootfs there needs no verity because our initramfs mounts it, not Android's fs_mgr. (2) metadata ext4 noatime,nosuid,nodev,discard,sync formattable. (3) userdata ext4 errors=panic,noatime,nosuid,nodev,barrier=1,noauto_da_alloc, latemount,wait,check,formattable, fileencryption=ice:aes-256-heh (UFS inline crypto), eraseblk=16777216, logicalblk=4096, quota, reservedsize=128M, checkpoint=block: userdata is encrypted by the UFS inline-crypto engine; our image leaves ICE out (decision 2026-11-19-walleye-ufs-match-no-ice-no-linkstartup), so old userdata is unreadable to us and needs no preserving, and the formattable flag means Android re-formats it itself. (4) misc is emmc type, no slot. (5) modem mounts at /firmware vfat ro, slotselect: the modem image is per slot, as our read of modem_b found. (6) The UFS host is soc/1da4000.ufshc, by-name under it: the controller address our dts uses. (7) zram swap 2 GiB, 8 streams. No vendor line: where Android 11 mounts vendor from is not known yet. boot, dtbo and vbmeta are not in the fstab (the bootloader reads them).
init.recovery.hardware.rc: only waits for /dev/block/platform/soc/${ro.boot.bootdevice}, symlinks it as /dev/block/bootdevice and sets sys.usb.configfs 1: nothing about slots.
recovery.wipe: Google's own recovery wipes, in order, system_a, system_b, vendor_a, vendor_b, userdata, then boot_a and boot_b last so that all partitions are wiped correctly even if interrupted: Google itself treats these slot partitions as wipeable, boot last, and the way back is Google's public factory image. This supports stage 1 writing system_<other> and stage 2 writing boot_<slot>, and gives the order to keep: never leave a slot with a new boot and no system.
ELIXIR (ProjectElixir-Devices/device_google_walleye, branch udc, 2024; relayed by the walleye coordinator, its page not read by me): its fstab.hardware and gpt-utils are its own repartitioning; the commit says walleye and taimen require repartitioning and defines product as A/B. That is not the stock layout and not our plan: the stock layout is Google's tree plus our own read-back (walleye-bootchain-readback). REPARTITIONING (a new GPT, a resized userdata or system) is a bigger step than walleye-install-stage-how-it-stands: the bootloader reads the GPT, no way back from a bad table is known, so it needs the author's word, and only then. Its proprietary-firmware.txt lists are for the later firmware step (item walleye-device-config-sources-read). Consequence: the plan is unchanged; stages 1 and 2 stand; a loopback rootfs.img in userdata stays the way to more room without a GPT edit.

brief: Stage 2 vs Android OTA: flash boot_other plus set_active equals the OTA's own steps in kind, BUT set_active IS a GPT write (attributes, type GUIDs, UFS boot LUN): named difference, coordinator's call
question: Does flashing our boot into the slot Android is not on and set_active with boot counting do anything Android's own OTA does not?
found: VERDICT: no step of ours is outside what Android's OTA does, with ONE named fact the standing rule must see: fastboot set_active (and the OTA's setActiveBootSlot) is a write to the GPT. (1) OTA: update_engine writes boot_<other> (and the rest of that slot), the HAL then calls setSlotAsUnbootable/setActiveBootSlot; the Qualcomm HAL (hardware/qcom/bootctrl, boot_control.cpp) sets attribute bits in the GPT entries of every A/B partition on every LUN, recomputes the GPT CRCs, and on UFS switches the boot LUN (xbl_a/xbl_b) through gpt_utils_set_xbl_boot_partition; markBootSuccessful sets the successful bit of the running slot, called by Android after a boot completes (update_verifier then the HAL). (2) Fastboot set_active (CAF ABL, CmdSetActive and SwitchPtnSlots, the stand-in for walleye's proprietary ABL): boot_<x> gets active+priority+retry count 7, successful and unbootable cleared; the other slot loses active and priority; SwitchPtnSlots swaps the partition TYPE GUIDS of every _a/_b pair; on UFS it sets the boot LUN; UpdatePartitionAttributes rewrites both GPT headers and entries with CRCs. At boot FindBootableSlot decrements the retry count of an unconfirmed slot and marks it unbootable at zero, then the other slot boots: that is the fall back, and it writes the GPT every boot of a try. (3) So our one command (flash boot_<other>, set_active other) does exactly the OTA's two moves; the way back (set_active <android>) is the same call; the fall back is the bootloader's own. Named difference: the GPT write is done by the bootloader's code, not ours, but it is a GPT write, and the lane's rule says GPT never: the verdict goes to the coordinator, not a go. AVB (item 2): not read from the phone's ABL (proprietary); known from the lane's readings: unlocked, orange state allowed, our boot image carries the AVB footer and passes the lane's AVB check; whether stock vbmeta flags must be disabled is NOT KNOWN yet: read-only check: fastboot getvar slot-successful/unbootable/retry-count for both slots before and after a RAM boot (a RAM boot must change none), and getvar all twice identical. NOT READ: walleye's real ABL (Google build), its HAL build (Lineage wahoo uses qcom-caf bootctrl; stock used a Qualcomm bootctrl of the same family): behaviour measured, not source, is the proof: the ONE cheap check is the slot flags read before and after.

brief: VERDICT stage 3: with nodiscard, no fstrim, no mkfs, ufs_bsg unopened and the purge guard, our kernel sends the card no command class Android's did not; named differences are power/speed only
question: Does our kernel's write path to the UFS card (SK hynix H28U74301AMR D003) do anything Android's UFS path on this phone does not: UNMAP, purge, erase, quirks, write booster, power?
found:
VERDICT: our kernel does nothing Android's did not, in command classes. Named differences are power and speed, none a command to the card. Read-only study of Google's wahoo 4.4 (android-msm-wahoo-4.4-android11 @52750b8f, GPL, clean room: facts only) against our v7.3 tree (3644090c7); nothing run on the phone.

(1) COMMAND CLASSES on a plain ext4 rw mount, write and unmount, our options (ro->rw of ONE partition, nodiscard, no fstrim, no mkfs/resize):
- WRITE(10)/READ(10) with FUA and flush: sd layer in both, same; Android's ext4/f2fs on userdata sends them all day.
- SYNCHRONIZE CACHE: from ext4 journal commits (preflush) and sd shutdown; both kernels, same.
- UNMAP: only from the filesystem (mount option discard, fstrim, mkfs, resize). Ours: none of them, the mount is nodiscard (ext4 default is off) and the procedure never runs mkfs or fstrim. Android DID send UNMAP (live counters: one UNMAP in normal operation, research walleye-ufs-android-way), we send none: fewer, not more. WRITE SAME (which could carry UNMAP, used by blkdev zeroout) is switched off by sdev->no_write_same=1 in BOTH ufshcd.c versions.
- PURGE: Android never sets fPurgeEnable (live: flags set fDeviceInit only). Ours: the only setters are the ufs_bsg RPMB purge path and the raw query path; our init never opens ufs_bsg, and both are behind ufshcd_purge_refused (UFS_DEVICE_QUIRK_NO_PURGE on this model, ufshcd.c:3465..3506 and 7692, ufs-qcom.c:1315). Equal in effect, stricter in guard.
- START STOP UNIT: runtime autosuspend of the LUN and system suspend/shutdown; Android sets sdev->autosuspend_delay and runs the same START_STOP to the device WLUN (ufshcd_set_dev_pwr_mode); mainline adds rpm_autosuspend = 1 (cap UFSHCD_CAP_RPM_AUTOSUSPEND). Same command, same card state (SLEEP/ACTIVE), different timing. HARMLESS.
- Background operations: both kernels enable auto-BKOPS only through the UFSHCD_CAP_AUTO_BKOPS_SUSPEND path (bBackgroundOpsEn attribute): same.
- Write booster: our host caps carry WB_EN and WB_WITH_CLK_SCALING, Android's 4.4 has no write-booster code. But ufshcd_wb_probe (ufshcd.c:8551) probes it only for wSpecVersion >= 0x310 or 0x220 or the SUPPORT_EXTENDED_FEATURES quirk; this card is UFS 2.1 (hba->ufs_version 0x210, device spec 0x0210) and has no such quirk (our tables: SAVECONFIGTIME for any Hynix, plus the model entry), so WB is disabled and no WB flag or attribute is ever written. EQUAL by the card's version.
- ERASE / secure erase / DISCARD with secure bit: not in either path; sd only issues it on a filesystem request. None.

(2) QUIRKS and the Sony mechanism: as each kernel applies them, this card gets HOST_PA_SAVECONFIGTIME on both (mainline's core table matches every Hynix; Android's matching entry), and ours adds the NO_PURGE guard. Sony's three quirks (DELAY_BEFORE_LPM, EXTEND_SYNC_LENGTH 0x48, one TX lane) are in neither (decision 2026-11-19-walleye-ufs-no-sync-length-quirk). Sony's mechanism is NOT PUBLISHED (research walleye-ufs-gap-sony-mechanism-public-record): the SODP view (bug 802) ties a loss to fPurgeEnable being set, with the sync-length setting a guess. A Sony-class lockup, as published, needs a purge request; our configuration cannot send one by any path read here (no ufs_bsg open, guard on the query builder, nodiscard, no fstrim, no erase path), and a plain write has no way to set it. Open honestly: the Pixel 2's card firmware D003 may react to something unlisted; Android's own year of writes on the same card with the same link settings is the evidence this is not the case here.

(3) LINK and power: Android reaches HS-G3 2 lanes rate B; mainline negotiates the same as far as read (the read-only try shows it). Android 4.4 also scales gear (ufshcd_scale_gear, ufshcd.c:9651 of the vendor tree) and clocks and has hibern8 and clock gating; ours adds no extra command, only different thresholds (no OPP table in msm8998.dtsi, no bus votes). Whether gear scaling under load behaves is exactly what item walleye-ufs-try-2 measures (power_info and devfreq under a bounded O_DIRECT read). Not known yet: nothing about writes, only speed.

(4) THE ONE TESTED COMMAND (walleye-install-rw-write-test, builder to write, keeper to run): ONE partition (system_a or system_b, the slot Android is not on, named by walleye.root and refused if it is the running slot), blockdev --setrw only that node, mount -t ext4 -o rw,nodiscard,noatime, a bounded write (a few hundred MB through dd conv=fsync and sync), umount, sync, fsck.ext4 -fn clean; the bootchain read-back (bootchain-readback.sh) before and after, bootchain-readback-check.sh must find every sha256 equal; the GPT digests before and after (read by Android and by us). Way back: the partition is rewritten from its verified backup (the install stage 1 dd and read-back); the bootloader files and GPT are never written so they need no way back; if the checks fail the phone is left charging in Android and the Top Coordinator is told. Never: erase, purge, discard, fstrim, mkfs, the GPT, xbl, abl or any bootloader partition.

(5) VERDICT: our kernel does nothing Android's did not, for this step. Named differences (none a storage command): runtime-autosuspend timing, gear-scaling thresholds, no bus votes, ICE absent, PHY table of the sdm845 family; Android sends UNMAP, we do not. NOT KNOWN YET: the Lineage fork's UFS code (the running 4.4.302; Google's stock branch was read, as in the earlier android-way research), the card's own firmware reaction to any command, and discard capability of the LUN as the SCSI layer sees it (not in the saved sysfs). None of these is a command we would send. Stop rule held: no bootloader partition, GPT, erase or purge is needed by the step.

brief: 'reboot bootloader' never reached the kernel: busybox reboot drops the argument, so no reboot reason was written. The PMIC byte our dtb writes equals Android's; IMEM word and warm reset are unknown
question: Why did 'reboot bootloader' over ssh not reach fastboot on our kernel (rerun 6), and what must our kernel write?
found: (1) Android (wahoo msm-poweroff.c, msm_restart_prepare): for cmd 'bootloader' it writes PMIC PON 0x800+0x8F bits7:1 = 2 (qpnp_pon_set_restart_reason, PM8998 is gen2: byte 0x04) AND the IMEM word 0x77665500 at 0x146bf000+0x65c (dtsi restart_reason@65c), and any non-empty cmd gives a WARM reset (qpnp_pon_system_pwr_off WARM_RESET) then deasserts PS_HOLD. Which of the two the bootloader reads is NOT KNOWN YET (ABL is closed). (2) Our kernel: restart is PSCI SYSTEM_RESET (cold unless reboot=warm; psci.c), no msm-poweroff, no pshold node; mainline qcom-pon.c with pm8998-pon shift 1 writes the same PMIC byte (mode-bootloader <2> => 2<<1) from a reboot notifier that runs before the restart handler, but ONLY if the kernel receives the string 'bootloader'. (3) The cause found: the image is Alpine with busybox init; busybox 'reboot' ignores its arguments and signals init with SIGTERM, init calls reboot(RB_AUTOBOOT): LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART with no command. reboot-mode then finds no command and writes nothing, so the PMIC byte was never written in rerun 6 - the dtb and config were never tested by that run. (4) The kept log has one line only (bootloader-way-back.txt); no kernel line from the reboot was kept (the phone has no console on that path): the claim rests on the busybox source, not on a print. (5) Smallest change: send the command string through reboot(2) LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART2 'bootloader' (a small static tool in the rootfs, no dts change); this exercises the PMIC byte alone. If the bootloader still does not stop: add the IMEM word with a syscon-reboot-mode node (offset 0x65c, mode-bootloader 0x77665500, IMEM 0x146bf000 mapped as syscon) and/or reboot=warm so PSCI uses SYSTEM_RESET2/warm. (6) NOT KNOWN YET: whether PMIC byte alone suffices; whether a cold PSCI reset keeps the PMIC byte (Android used warm); whether IMEM is writable from EL1 under this firmware.

brief: Stage 2 cannot brick, but the forced way back alone leans on an unmeasured count-zero fall back (set_active gives retry 1 here, not 7); a hard hang needs a hand. Not enough to open the go alone
question: Can stage 2 (flash boot_a, set_active a) be made safe on the forced way back alone, with the bootloader's A/B boot-count fallback?
found: ARGUMENT, from what the lane measured and the sources; nothing was run on the phone for this row. (1) THE FORCED WAY BACK TODAY: from the booted image the lab sends 'reboot -f', then 'echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger'; in rerun 6 it returned the phone to Android slot b with no hand. That was stage 1 (fastboot boot, slot b still active), so the bootloader picked b. AFTER stage 2 set_active a, a forced reboot lands on a AGAIN, our image, not Android: the forced reboot alone is not the way back; the bootloader's counter is. (2) THE COUNTER, MEASURED ON THIS PHONE: set_active X gives X priority 3, successful no, unbootable no, retry-count 1 (research walleye-first-fastboot-boot, 2026-11-17: 'after: current a, a unbootable no/successful no/retry 1'), NOT the 7 of the Qualcomm source and pmaports MR 3190: Google's ABL differs. A normal boot of an unconfirmed slot decrements it: set-active a then Android on a left a successful yes retry 0, b retry 1. The slot not made active keeps its flags (b successful yes after set-active a, seen in the 2026-11-17 state reads). Expected run: boot 1 of ours (a retry 1 to 0); one forced reboot; boot 2: a is unsuccessful at retry 0, the bootloader marks it unbootable and boots b, Android, no hand and no bootloader mode; a stays unbootable until the next set_active a. NOT MEASURED: what the bootloader does on the boot after retry reaches 0 on a slot that is unsuccessful and loaded fine. Measured only: after Load Errors a showed unbootable yes retry 0 and, with b unsuccessful too, the phone stayed in fastboot (reachable by the lab: set_active b, no hand). (3) BRANCHES. A boot_a written wrong (read-back differs): the procedure stops before set_active; b still active; nothing to undo, boot_a is the unused slot's. B set_active fails: flags read again; if not as before, set_active b by the lab's fastboot; a half-written GPT is the bootloader's atomicity, NOT KNOWN YET, the same risk as every OTA. C image refused (AVB, Load Error): the source marks a unbootable and boots b by cold reset: Android; if both end unbootable the phone waits in fastboot: set_active b by the lab. D kernel boots and panics (panic=10): reboot, counter as in (2): Android on boot 2. E kernel boots, ssh answers, run completes: forced reboot, boot 2 is Android on b; the lab reads the flags (a unbootable, b successful yes); the procedure's explicit 'set_active b from the image' cannot be used because 'reboot bootloader' does not reach fastboot (rerun 6, cause not known yet). F kernel boots but ssh does not answer (network, not a hang): the image's own self-reboot timer (decision on hang outcomes: reboot -f after 240 s unless /tmp/hold) restarts it: boot 2 as in (2); no hand. G hard hang, or reboot -f and sysrq b both ignored (the c3 case): NEEDS A HAND. The PMIC watchdog does not remove it: the v1 bite is a hard reset (type 7) and with the USB cable in the bootloader then shows its charging screen and waits for a short power press (research of the 2026-11-20 bite); warm type 1 may avoid that, unproven. After the press, boot 2 is Android by the counter. (4) NOT KNOWN YET and the smallest try: (a) the flags set_active leaves on b and the retry value on a: the rehearsal item walleye-install-flash-boot-rehearsal reads both slots' slot-retry-count, slot-successful, slot-unbootable before (read only); only the real set_active shows them after; (b) the behaviour at retry 0: only a counted boot shows it, which is stage 2 itself, whose worst case is a hand on the power key, never a state fastboot cannot repair; (c) whether Google's ABL decrements for a slot set by set_active in the same session. (5) RECOMMENDATION: the forced way back alone is NOT enough to open the go. It is safe from a brick (boot_a is the unused slot, Android's b is untouched and successful, fastboot is reachable, no bootloader partition, the GPT written only by the bootloader's own set_active) but it leans on an unmeasured count-zero fall back, and its only no-hand exit is a live kernel. Open the go after the rehearsal has read the flags and the restart2 tool (walleye-reboot-reason-restart2-tool) has been tried once in RAM: if 'reboot bootloader' then reaches fastboot, the way back is the lab's explicit set_active b and the counter is the second path; if not, the go may still be given with the Top Coordinator accepting that the residual cost is a hand on the power key (branch G), not a brick. The go stays CLOSED here.

brief: SLPI carve-out: the image needs 15 MiB (relocatable); the phone's layout is 0x94c00000/0xf00000; our 7 MiB node is too small

Walleye's own dtbo and running fdt put pil_slpi_mem at 0x94c00000/0xf00000 (other dtbo entries 0x94b00000/0xf00000, source dtsi and mainline 0x94300000/0xf00000): the size is 15 MiB everywhere; our dts holds 7 MiB at 0x94b00000, too small by 8 MiB, and the overlay never overwrites it because our pil_slpi_mem is a stub label. The block 0x94c00000-0x95b00000 swallows our inherited ipa_fw/ipa_gsi/gpu/wlan_msa nodes (0x95200000-0x957fffff): delete them, add the running layout's ipa/gpu 0x95b00000/1 MiB, shift mba to 0x94500000 and video to 0x94700000. Vendor SSC node matches mainline's remoteproc_slpi on interrupt 390, pas-id 12, px=lvs2, cx via SSCCX, smp2p pid 3; mainline reg is 0x5800000 where the vendor says 0x5c00000 (NOT KNOWN YET which is right). brief: Why the shell goes silent about 4.5 s into a sustained O_DIRECT read: the first gear switch is cleared; 5 causes ranked, none settled; cause not known yet
question: Why do the phone's shell and usb network go silent under a sustained read of sda, after 7-8 answered samples, and what ONE try with no new risk tells the causes apart?
found: WHAT THE LOGS COUNT (ufs-20261123-085319 and -105319, ufs-try2-run3.log): the host went to HS_GEAR3 / 200 MHz core clock at the first sample (0.5 s) and held it for every answered sample (run 2: 8 up to 4.6 s; run 3: 7 up to 4.0 s, answered in 0.1 s), 2 lanes, rate B, link ACTIVE; then silence from the 4.6 s read on in both, six reads unanswered over 110 s. Same moment in all runs: a fixed time or volume after the load starts, not chance. Idle the same phone answered for minutes (the link read took 171 s). The first run (080827) had no load samples. After the failure the file shows dev_pm SLEEP, link HIBERN8, gear 1: the card was idle when that last read was made; whether the shell came back is NOT KNOWN YET (the run log only says no answer within limit+60 s). The phone printed nothing after the samples: no kernel text from the stall exists. Runs 1 and 2 logs are not in ~/lab-material (only ufs-try2-run3.log). THE CAUSES, ranked: (1) [cleared as stated] a gear or clock switch hangs: the up-switch at the load start finished (ufs-qcom notify = hibern8 enter, timers, core clk ctrl, hibern8 exit), so only a LATER switch is left: ufshcd's devfreq (100 ms poll, simple_ondemand) may scale down and up again when the queue drains between 1 MiB requests; each switch holds the scaling lock, waits up to 1 s for the doorbell and freezes new requests (ufshcd_clock_scaling_prepare) - a stuck second switch would stall the I/O, but not the usb gadget, unless the stall is a bus hang from touching a register while the clock is off: rank 1 for that form. (2) a stuck-asserted completion interrupt (irq 265 level-high) or a storm: all SPIs default to CPU 0 with the usb gadget's; 1 MiB direct reads give only hundreds of interrupts a second, so only a never-cleared status bit starves CPU 0; rank 2. (3) NEW, not in the item: the missing bus votes. ufshc has no interconnects; Android voted the fabric for the UFS traffic; at gear 3 the unvoted fabric (snoc/bimc left as the bootloader set it) could starve the usb gadget's DMA and the cpu's: slow, deterministic after the buffer-sized time; rank 3 - against it: the OnePlus 5 on mainline uses the same node and the same missing votes and reads its root from UFS (wiki, dts series), so the shared path is not enough to hang and the difference is OURS (the diagnostic kernel config, clk_ignore_unused, the init's watchdog petter and its starvation, the card's quirks, the RST_n pulse). (4) a watchdog bite after our petter starves: the petter is a bounded one in the root init; a starved petter would end in a warm reset and Android back by itself, which is what the phone does; rank 2 or 3 and CHEAP to test by reading the PON reason on the way back. (5) O_DIRECT memory effect (bs=1M pins 1 MiB, nothing grows) and the usb network's own bulk path: lowest; the shell is polled over the same usb that would have to die first, so (d) cannot be told from the rest by the poll alone. WHAT SETTLES WHICH: a log that survives the stall, and one variable at a time. The ramoops chase has not yet shown that a warm reset keeps our kernel's text (walleye-pk5l2-tried; the item walleye-ramoops-after-unlock waits for the author's unlock), so the log is written BEFORE each step to the phone's RAM and read back over the same link only while it answers; a second channel that survives is not known yet.

brief: Documented: AOSP's bootloader spec says writing a slot's partition clears successful and resets the retry count; run 1's 0->1 and yes->no match set_active X's state (retry 1, successful no)
question: Is it the bootloader's documented behaviour that fastboot flash of a slot's boot partition resets that slot's tries and successful bit? Do rerun 7 and stage 2 run 1 agree?
found: DOCUMENTED. AOSP 'Implement OTA updates' (Support for slots) says: 'When modifying a partition that's part of a slot, the bootloader clears successfully booted and resets the retry count for the slot.' set_active (and the HAL's setActiveBootSlot) additionally changes the active slot and clears slot-unbootable (the only way to clear it). So the flash changing the flashed slot's flags is specified behaviour, not an anomaly; check 18, which forbade any flag change, was too strict and should allow exactly: flashed slot successful yes->no and retry reset to a positive value, nothing else (other slot, unbootable, current-slot unchanged). OBSERVED AGREES: stage 2 run 1 after flash of a: retry 0->1, successful yes->no, unbootable no, b unchanged, current b; the first-fastboot-boot material (2026-11-17, quoted in walleye-stage2-forced-way-back-argument-finding) after set_active X: retry 1, successful no, unbootable no (priority 3). Same flags after the flash as after set_active, apart from the active slot, which the flash did not change. The reset value is 1 here, not the spec's 'usually 3' (Google's ABL differs, already noted). NOT SHOWN: priority after the flash (getvar does not print it), so 'same as set_active' holds for retry, successful and unbootable only. Not read: Google's ABL source (not open for walleye) and update_engine's code; the spec page was enough. Plain sentence: documented (AOSP spec), and observed on this phone to match.

brief: Why slot a gave no ssh after a normal boot: ranked causes (bootloader-armed watchdog, cold USB, no start at all, init path) and ONE try that tells them apart: set_active a again, read pstore at once
question: Why did slot a not answer ssh after a normal boot of image e337de53 when fastboot boot of the same kernel (c3373d71, stage 1) did, in run 4?
found: FACTS (read in this lab, no phone): (1) Stage 1 from RAM: ssh login answered about 12 s after the boot started (rootfs-boots-run-7.log 31->32), so the 170 s window is not too short. (2) Same kernel, dtb and init in both; the stage 2 image differs by the word walleye.booted-slot and the bootloader's added words. (3) bootreason=watchdog (AOSP: the bootloader's reading of a hardware watchdog reset) with no panic= on our command line: something bit; a stuck kernel does not reset by itself. (4) A bite with the cable in boots the charger screen in our own earlier PMIC-wdt try (walleye-wdt-reset-boots-charger-mode), here the bootloader fell to b by itself: the fall-back came from the retry counter (slot a retry 1 before set_active, 0 and unbootable after), not a power press. (5) The dts has kpss-wdt (0x17817000) and pm8998_wdt enabled with wakeup-source but our init opens neither (the stage 2 init is the root's OpenRC), so no software of ours arms a watchdog. NOT KNOWN YET: whether our kernel started (pstore empty because the phone rebooted before it was read), when the bite came. RANKING by what each explains and its cost to test: (b-wdt) 1st: the bootloader arms the apps watchdog for a normal boot (it hands it to Android's msm_watchdog, which pets it) and does not for fastboot boot; our kernel never pets it, so it bites after tens of seconds: explains bootreason=watchdog, the fall-back, and why the same kernel is fine from RAM. Also fits a kernel that was running but the gadget never up. Test: pstore console after the next try: our init lines then a cut-off; and the stock fdt's qcom,bark-time and pet-time read from Android b (read-only). (b-usb) 2nd: cold USB: dwc3/qusb2phy from a cold start (in fastboot boot the bootloader's USB is up and handed over; a normal boot has it off). Cannot explain bootreason=watchdog alone (a missing gadget does not reset the phone) unless (b-wdt) also holds, so it ranks with (b-wdt), not above. Test: the same pstore: dwc3/udc lines and the gadget unit's lines after the root mount. (a) 3rd: the words root=PARTUUID, init=/init, want_initramfs, rootwait, ro: with an initramfs the kernel ignores root=, runs /init as the init= word says; our init reads only androidboot.slot_suffix (_a) and walleye.* words, so low. Same pstore shows it (init line mounts-the-booted-slot). (c) 4th: dtbo_idx=3 overlay on a normal boot: the same dtbo stage 1 got from the matched build; whether fastboot boot applies it is not known yet; a missing overlay changes nodes, shows in the kernel log. (d) 5th: AVB orange with algorithm NONE: an unlocked device boots a failed check with a warning (orange); the measured boottime SW:10024 ms in Android's own orange boot is the warning screen wait. A refusal would be Load Error (seen with stage-1-like images: walleye-try-s1-gadget-up) and no reset, so it does not explain the watchdog. (e) init booted-slot path never run on hardware: only a guard that fails closed (refuse), not a reset by itself. TO TELL APART with ONE try and no flash (boot_a already holds e337de53): the keeper makes slot a active again (fastboot set_active a, which gives slot a its tries back), waits for the fall-back to Android b WITHOUT any reboot of b, and reads /sys/fs/pstore/console-ramoops by adb root at once (ramoops 0xa1100000 is in our dts as in the stock one; the kernel prints into it). What it must show: NO file or no kernel lines = the kernel never started or ramoops not kept: candidates (c),(d),(e) or the region not surviving the bite (then the t3 proof walleye-pstore-t3 decides: its marker). Our lines up to the root mount and the usb-gadget unit then a cut-off = our kernel ran: (b-wdt) when the last line time is under about 60 s and no dwc3 error; (b-usb) when dwc3/qusb2 errors or no udc line appear; a refuse line = (e). Read-only, from Android b, before that: the stock fdt's watchdog nodes (/proc/device-tree wdt bark/pet), the stock kernel cmdline above, nothing else. Material: research/walleye-bootimage/2026-11-23/.

brief: fastboot reboot stayed in fastboot 240 s: ranked (a) our PMIC reason byte persists, (b) bootloader rule, (c) slot state, (d) USB; smallest try: fastboot reboot twice, timed
question: Why did 'fastboot reboot' leave the phone in fastboot for 240 s after our kernel reached the bootloader by RESTART2 (rerun 7), and what is the reliable last leg?
found:
Kept facts (rerun 7, run log and out): stage 1's kernel took the phone to fastboot by RESTART2 'bootloader'; fastboot listed it, current-slot b = start; `fastboot reboot` was sent (log clock 10:24:36; the row's 10:21:16 is another clock); check 22 failed at 10:28:37, 240 s later, the host saying the phone was in fastboot. Slot flags, GPTs and boot chain equal after. The after-stop way back (lab.rs way_back: in fastboot it sends `fastboot reboot` again, then shell legs) brought Android home; its own lines were not kept, so the number of resets and the time it took are NOT KNOWN YET (the row's 'up about 10:34' is an uptime estimate).
Public source (generic LK, Google/CAF; walleye's bootloader is closed, its being LK-derived is NOT KNOWN YET): fastboot reboot = reboot_device(0), reboot-bootloader = reboot_device(FASTBOOT_MODE), continue is a separate command that boots the active slot without a reset. LK reads the IMEM restart word and zeroes it at once; it reads PON_SOFT_RB_SPARE and scrubs only bits 7:5 (value & 0x1f). Our byte (mode-bootloader 2 at shift 1 = 0x04, bit 2) lies outside bits 7:5, and the PMIC register lives through warm and cold resets; only if walleye's bootloader scrubs it too does it clear.
Ranking: (a) the reason our RESTART2 wrote persists and sends the next reset(s) back to fastboot - FIRST: it explains why the phone was in fastboot after a reset that Android's own reboot would not have sent there, and an LK-style scrub that is one boot late would also explain why a second `fastboot reboot` (after-stop way back) worked; against it: the after-stop count of resets is unmeasured. (b) fastboot reboot re-enters fastboot after a bootloader-requested entry as a bootloader rule - SECOND: indistinguishable from (a) by the rerun alone; the public LK has no such rule. (c) slot or retry state - THIRD, weak: flags equal before and after, b successful yes, and the stage 1 run flashed nothing; but retry 0 is not excluded for the slot the bootloader would pick. (d) USB or timing - LAST: 240 s of the host seeing a listed phone is not a late enumeration.
The tries, each read-only or RAM-only, one phone excursion each: (1) the same excursion, at fastboot send `fastboot continue` instead of `reboot`: Android within 240 s = the last leg that needs no reset, and if it also fails the cause is not the register (b/c/d). (2) the same excursion with `fastboot reboot` twice, each timed: Android only after the second = (a) with a one-boot-late scrub (and the way back's last leg is 'reboot twice'); both stay in fastboot = (b) or (c). (3) read PMIC PON_SOFT_RB_SPARE (0x88F) from our kernel before the RESTART2 and once more on the next boot of our image after a 'fastboot continue'/reboot (regmap read, no write): the byte 0x04 present after the first reset = (a) proved. Order: (2) first: it needs no new tool and its two timings settle (a) vs (b)/(c); then (1). The reliable last leg known to work today: a second `fastboot reboot` (what the after-stop way back did), untimed.

brief: Kernel petting is in e337de53 and probes; stock bark 11 s/pet 10 s are Android's, not the bootloader's; our init's first echo ends kernel petting; bootloader timing NOT KNOWN YET
question: Does e337de53 already carry kernel-level watchdog petting and why would it fail; what does the stock fdt say; what does qcom-wdt do; how long does a kernel have?
found:
ANSWERS, each with its line. Host reads and read-only adb on Android b (slot _b, root, nothing written, no reboot).
(1) THE MECHANISM IS IN e337de53. Image sha256 e337de53... (the file in walleye-build, unpacked with unpack_bootimg): its appended dtb has /soc@0/watchdog@17817000 compatible qcom,kpss-wdt, reg <0x17817000 0x1000>, interrupts <0 3 1> (SPI 3, edge rising), a clock (the sleep clock), no status, no timeout-sec. Kernel config of the tree's three .config (walleye-build out-ufsm, out-ufsm2, out-ufsroot; which one built e337de53 is not recorded: NOT KNOWN YET, all three agree): CONFIG_WATCHDOG=y, WATCHDOG_CORE=y, WATCHDOG_HANDLE_BOOT_ENABLED=y (line 5055), # WATCHDOG_NOWAYOUT is not set, QCOM_WDT=y (line 5095). The header's command line has panic=5 (not 'no panic=': the row walleye-stage2-slot-a-no-ssh-causes-ranked says none). PROBES: no kernel log of e337de53 or of stage 1 (c3373d71) keeps a qcom_wdt line (read.txt of rootfs-boots-20261123-101812 has none: NOT KNOWN YET for this image); the SAME driver and node in the earlier images do probe: /proc/iomem '17817000-17817fff : 17817000.watchdog', /proc/interrupts 'GICv3 35 Edge wdt_bark' (SPI 3 = 35), /sys/class/watchdog/watchdog0 under soc@0/17817000.watchdog (research walleye-first-fastboot-boot c2/z6/z7 read/, lab-material pmic-wdt-20261118-*), and dmesg 'watchdog: watchdog0: watchdog did not stop!' every time our init's echo closed /dev/watchdog. So address, clock, irq and probe are not the failure on this phone's kernel line.
(2) STOCK vs OURS (read on Android b: /proc/device-tree/soc/qcom,wdt@17817000): compatible qcom,msm-watchdog; reg 0x17817000 size 0x1000 (reg-names wdt-base); interrupts <0 3 0> and <0 4 0> (SPI 3 bark, SPI 4 bite, type 0); qcom,bark-time 0x2af8 = 11000 ms; qcom,pet-time 0x2710 = 10000 ms; qcom,ipi-ping, qcom,wakeup-enable, qcom,scandump-size 0x40000. Ours: same base and size, bark SPI 3 (type edge rising, as mainline dts use), no bite irq (mainline does not use it), clock sleep_clk (32768 Hz; the stock driver assumes WDT_HZ 32765). Register layout: the stock driver's WDT0_RST 0x04, EN 0x08, STS 0x0C, BARK 0x10, BITE 0x14 equals qcom,kpss-wdt's table (qcom-wdt.c reg_offset_data_kpss), so the layout fits. No field differs in a way that stops the driver.
THE 11 s / 10 s ARE THE ANDROID KERNEL'S, NOT THE BOOTLOADER'S: watchdog_v2.c lines 743-744 write bark = bark-time and bite = bark-time + 3 s (so 11 s / 14 s) and its probe enables the watchdog; the node says nothing about what the bootloader armed. What the bootloader arms before the kernel, and for how long, is NOT KNOWN YET: it is closed, the bootloader_log node (htc,bldr_log, two regions 0xa1300000 and 0xa1380000, 0x80000 each) cannot be read from Android (no /dev/mem). A SECURE watchdog (SCM_SVC_SEC_WDOG_DIS in the stock driver) is a second, separate possibility: the non-secure kernel cannot pet it.
(3) WHAT OUR KERNEL DOES (qcom-wdt.c v7.3, topic tree lines 346-351, 80-86; the coordinator's 331-333 are another tree): probe: if WDT_EN bit 0 is set (is_running) it calls qcom_wdt_start, which stops, then reprograms with OURS: timeout 30 s (min(max,30)), pretimeout 1 (an irq was found): bark 29 s, bite 30 s, enables, and sets WDOG_HW_RUNNING - so a bootloader-armed apps watchdog gets a FRESH 30 s from probe, its own times replaced. The core then pets it (watchdog_need_worker: timeout set, not active, hw_running) every timeout/2 = 15 s, UNTIL userspace activates it. A watchdog the bootloader did NOT arm is never armed by the driver: only an open of /dev/watchdog starts it (then bark 29 / bite 30).
THE CATCH, in our own init (build/initramfs-root/init, lines 57-65 and 86-93): its wait loop does 'echo > /dev/watchdog' once per second ONLY while the partition is not yet found. That echo OPENS the device (the core: activated, kernel petting stops), writes (a pet) and closes without the magic 'V' ('did not stop!' in every log): the watchdog is now ACTIVE with no worker, so from then on only userspace pets, 30 s per pet. The loop ends when the partition appears; between that last pet and the handover the init mounts, builds the overlay and copies busybox; after switch_root the pets exist only if someone runs /.walleye/hold.sh (the init writes it; nothing in this repository starts it: NOT KNOWN YET whether system_a's own init does). If the partition is found on the loop's first pass the device is never opened and the kernel's own petting goes on (if the watchdog was armed at all). So: kernel-level petting is IN the image, probes, and is not what fails; it covers only the time before our init first opens /dev/watchdog; after that the pets are the init's loop and hold.sh.
HOW LONG A KERNEL HAS: if the bootloader armed the apps watchdog: a fresh 30 s from our probe (a few seconds into the boot), then 15 s pets until the init's first open, then 30 s from each of the init's echoes. If it armed none, none until our open, then 30 s from the open. The bootloader's own time before probe: NOT KNOWN YET (bounded below by stage 1, where the same kernel needed about 12 s from the jump to ssh without a bite, and by the T3 try, where an unpetted node left the phone alive-class for 42 s).
FIT WITH RUN 7: reset about 35-40 s after the jump with bootreason watchdog fits 'init opened /dev/watchdog in its wait loop, the last pet came when the partition was found, nothing pets after the handover, bite 30 s later' as well as a bootloader-armed watchdog; but it does not explain why no gadget appeared in the first 12-20 s (stage 1's came about 12 s after the start). Either the kernel did not run well before the bite, or the Alpine side started late; the host's USB log is the only clock and shows nothing. The two readings tell apart by one thing the debug image already queued (walleye-stage2-debug-image) would show: a gadget and a pet from the first instant.
RECOMMENDED FOR THE TRY: (i) make the first act of our init a pet loop that lives for the whole boot (a background petter started before the partition wait, not inside it) and keep kernel petting out of the picture: after our first open the kernel stops anyway; (ii) leave the dts and the driver alone: they probe; (iii) do not assume bark 11 s: it is Android's. The first unknown it does not settle: whether a SECURE or PMIC watchdog bites instead (bootreason 'watchdog' is the bootloader's name for any of them): the debug image's USB and pet loop settle it by its own first 40 s.

brief: Of stage 2's 29 steps three assertions guard nothing (8 marker, 9 live content, 18 flashed-slot flags); fastboot and update_engine judge a slot by verification and counter, not prior content
question: Which of install-boot's 29 steps protect safety, and how do fastboot, update_engine and boot_control write a slot?
found: Table in research/walleye-bootimage/2026-11-23/stage2-checks-should-they-exist.md. Invariants: I1 other partitions untouched, I2 GPT only slot bits+CRC, I3 read-back, I4 way back + counter. fastboot flash asserts nothing of the target's old content and does not read back; update_engine marks the target unbootable first (download_action.cc l.199), verifies the target hash, sets active only after success: every flag state of the target is legal before the switch. Verdicts: DROP 8's marker refusal, 9's live-content assertion (keep backup-on-file), 18's flashed-slot flag assertion (keep Android slot's flags unchanged); RELAX 20, 29; the rest KEEP, 12 and 16 hardest. Flags 13/18/20/24 are the GPT bits 10/22/28 read: one nature two routes. Stops let through by asserting values of state the command changes. Not known yet: walleye ABL's vendor boot_control behaviour on set_active; stop 8's text.

Matched how: the commit id in /proc/version (research walleye-android-b-kernel-build: 4.4.302-g113bd1cfa6f5, built Nov 28 2025) was asked of GitHub: LineageOS/android_kernel_google_wahoo commit 113bd1cfa6f5a688e605307df2cb3c0ae49c0b6b (LuK1337, 2025-04-20, 'mm, vmstat: Skip DMA in is_zone_first_populated()') is the HEAD of branches lineage-22.0 and lineage-22.1 (git ls-remote); its Makefile says 4.4 SUBLEVEL 302, as the phone prints. So the phone runs a LineageOS 22 (Android 15) kernel on the wahoo msm-4.4 tree. Held as: remote 'android' = https://github.com/LineageOS/android_kernel_google_wahoo.git in ~/Projects/linux-phone-oco/linux, fetch of ONLY refs/heads/lineage-22.1, tagopt --no-tags, pushurl 'no-push-reference-only' (a push is refused), local tag reference/android-walleye/4.4.302-g113bd1cfa6f5 on that commit; never pushed (ls-remote origin shows no reference/* tag), never merged. Read back: git log -1 on the tag; drivers/soc/qcom/watchdog_v2.c exists (Copyright 2012-2017 The Linux Foundation, GPL version 2 only, no SPDX line); drivers/watchdog/msm_watchdog.c does NOT exist; the walleye dts are under arch/arm64/boot/dts/htc/ (overlay-walleye-xa_xb_xc.dts, overlay-walleye-xd_xe_a.dts, dsi-panel-walleye-s6e3fa5.dtsi, msm8998-touch-walleye-xa/xd.dtsi, batterydata-walleye*.dtsi); 56631 files. Licence: COPYING GPL-2.0; per-file headers decide. RULE: findings cite android:PATH@113bd1cfa6f5, read with git show reference/android-walleye/4.4.302-g113bd1cfa6f5:PATH; nothing is copied without the file's licence read (decision 2026-11-23-walleye-reuse-android-kernel-gpl). Not known yet: whether Google's tree and this one differ in the watchdog driver (Lineage merges stable 4.4.x into Google's).

brief: Our header command line is 149 characters now, 126 under the bootloader's cut; the init reads the slot from four sources and fails closed
question: How do we keep androidboot.slot_suffix from being cut off, and where else can the init read the slot?

The new header is 149 characters: margin 126 (build check). Android's fs_mgr reads the slot from the command line, then the device tree (firmware/android/slot_suffix), then bootconfig; the init does the same and takes root=PARTUUID=0000NNNN (partition number to PARTNAME) only as a last resort that must agree. Closed source: the ABL's own cmdline buffer size is not published, so 1363 stays the measured fact. Tested in QEMU: root=PARTUUID alone, agreeing, disagreeing, naming a non-system partition, and bootconfig; the device-tree line against a property file with its NUL. Not tested on a phone.

brief: Android's apps watchdog is one non-secure WDT0 armed at pure_initcall with bark 11 s/bite 14 s and pet 10 s; no secure-wdog call at boot; what the bootloader arms is NOT KNOWN YET
question: What arms which watchdog in Android's walleye kernel, which bites, and what must a mainline kernel do (reading android:PATH@113bd1cfa6f5, no phone)?
found:
READ from the local tree (tag reference/android-walleye/4.4.302-g113bd1cfa6f5, GPL-2.0, reuse allowed with authorship kept).
(1) android:drivers/soc/qcom/watchdog_v2.c@113bd1cfa6f5 (Copyright 2012-2017 The Linux Foundation; CONFIG_QCOM_WATCHDOG_V2=y in wahoo_defconfig:673). Registered as pure_initcall, so it runs before every device_initcall. Probe: kthread msm_watchdog (SCHED_FIFO max) created; init_watchdog_data: request bark irq (SPI 3, rising), configure_bark_dump (TZ regsave via SCM_SVC_UTIL SET_REGSAVE only when the dump table major version is 1, else msm_dump entries; its failure only means no register dump), then writes BARK = bark_time*WDT_HZ/1000 (WDT_HZ 32765), BITE = bark + 3*WDT_HZ, EN = BIT(EN) plus UNMASKED_INT_EN when qcom,wakeup-enable, RST = 1. It does NOT stop the watchdog first or read whether the bootloader armed it. Pet: a deferrable timer every pet_time wakes the kthread; with ipi-ping it first pings every other cpu (a cpu that does not answer = no pet = bark, bite 3 s later), then WDT0_RST = 1. A 12 s pet_observer only warns. Bark handler: msm_trigger_wdog_bite (BITE = 1 = immediate bite), panic fallback. Panic notifier: panic_timeout 0 = EN 0 (watchdog OFF), else bark/bite = (panic_timeout+10) s then RST. Suspend (suspend_noirq): RST = 1; with wakeup-enable it leaves EN set (the watchdog keeps running and its bark irq is a wake source), else EN = 0; resume re-enables and pets. The only secure-watchdog call is the sysfs 'disable' file: SCM_SVC_BOOT / SCM_SVC_SEC_WDOG_DIS (id 0x7) then EN = 0, written by userspace only; NOTHING in the boot path calls it and nothing pets any secure watchdog. So Android pets exactly one watchdog, the non-secure apps WDT0 at 0x17817000.
(2) DTS. android:arch/arm/boot/dts/qcom/msm8998.dtsi:2969 qcom,wdt@17817000: compatible qcom,msm-watchdog; reg 0x17817000 0x1000 'wdt-base'; interrupts <0 3 0>,<0 4 0> (bark, bite); bark-time 11000; pet-time 10000; qcom,ipi-ping; qcom,wakeup-enable; scandump-size 0x40000; no wdt-absent-base (so no cluster-1 watchdog disable); no qcom,userspace-watchdog (no user pet file). This equals what the prechecks row read from the live fdt. The walleye dts under arch/arm64/boot/dts/htc/ (overlay-walleye-*, BOARD_MUSKIE; msm8998-htc-common.dtsi, msm8998-htc-pm.dtsi) has NO watchdog node or override. PMIC: msm-pm8998.dtsi qcom,power-on@800 (qpnp-power-on) has pon_1 (power key), pon_2 (resin), pon_3 (kpdpwr+resin reset: s1-timer 6720 ms, s2-timer 2000 ms, s2-type DVDD_HARD_RESET); htc-pm.dtsi sets hard-reset-poweroff-type WARM_RESET and disables pon_1..3 (no key reports); qpnp-power-on.c has no PMIC-watchdog (PBS/PMIC_WD) ARMING code, only reads poff reasons ('Triggered from PMIC_WD', S3_RESET_PBS_WATCHDOG_TO). So in Android the kernel arms no PMIC watchdog; a PMIC watchdog (our pm8998_wdt node) is ours, not a thing Android has.
(3) HOW LONG A KERNEL HAS: the kernel side is 11 s bark / 14 s bite from the moment WDT0 is armed in pure_initcall, 10 s pets thereafter. From the source alone nothing can say what the bootloader armed or how long it gives the kernel: the sbl/xbl/abl code is proprietary and the bootloader_log regions are unreadable from Android. NOT KNOWN YET. Cheapest ways to show it (all read-only or RAM-only, queued for the keeper): read WDT0 EN/STS/BARK/BITE at the first instant of our kernel (earlycon-time register read, or a first-act read in init via /dev/mem if enabled) and compare to 0; on Android a cold boot with the driver's probe moved out is not possible, so the read from our kernel is the one.
(4) OURS AGAINST IT, field by field (our dt/msm8998-google-walleye.dts:96, node kpss-wdt): base/size equal; bark SPI 3 equal (type edge rising vs 0 = 'none'/hw default: the stock GIC takes the type from the driver's request, so rising is equal in effect); bite irq absent in ours (Android has it but its handler is not requested: the bite irq is only read by platform_get_irq, never used; equal); clock sleep_clk at 32768 vs 32765 (0.01%, irrelevant); no wakeup-enable: Android keeps the watchdog counting in suspend and uses the bark as a wake source, mainline qcom_wdt_suspend stops it (so a suspended mainline phone has NO apps watchdog: stricter on safety only if the bootloader's was armed and we stopped it); no ipi-ping (mainline has none; our pets come from the watchdog core's worker, which runs only if a cpu schedules: it covers a stuck scheduler, not a stuck other cpu); timeouts: ours 30 s (bark 29/bite 30, margin 1 s) against stock 11/14 (margin 3 s). Register layout equal (WDT0_RST 0x04, EN 0x08, STS 0x0C, BARK 0x10, BITE 0x14 = qcom_wdt reg_offset_data_kpss). Nothing differs in a way that stops the driver.
(5) THE FIX, as the smallest changes (the cause of the 35-40 s reset of run 7 is NOT proven by this reading, see walleye-stage2-watchdog-prechecks-read; these are what the source shows): (a) FIX-1, dts only: add timeout-sec = <30>; keep the node (already equal to Android in address/irq); no code reuse needed. (b) FIX-2, init: pet from the first instruction, as one process that lives to switch_root and is inherited (Android's equal is the kernel kthread, which does not depend on userspace at all): this is the mainline-faithful move because /dev/watchdog open and no V close arms a no-worker watchdog (prechecks row (3)). (c) FIX-3, optional kernel: the Android model is a kernel-side pet that does not stop when userspace opens: mainline equivalent = CONFIG_WATCHDOG_HANDLE_BOOT_ENABLED plus userspace never opening the device (then the core pets it forever), i.e. do not touch /dev/watchdog in the init at all when the bootloader's watchdog was running; based on android:watchdog_v2.c@113bd1cfa6f5 (idea only, no copy). (d) FIX-4, only if the first read of WDT0 shows it armed: reuse of the stock init sequence is not needed, qcom_wdt_start already rewrites bark/bite. (e) NOT to be reused: the panic notifier setting EN 0 when panic_timeout is 0 (it would hide a stuck boot; ours has panic=5) and the SCM disable (no secure watchdog proven).
(6) NOT KNOWN YET: what the bootloader arms and for how long (a read of WDT0 at the kernel's first instant would show it, no change to the phone); whether any secure watchdog exists (the stock driver's disable path suggests TZ has one, but Android never pets or disables it at boot, so it is either off by default or armed with a long time: it cannot be what bites a kernel in 35-40 s, a reading only, not proven); the first-instant state of the WDT0 EN register under our kernel.

brief: Wi-Fi on the WCN3990 is a QMI client of the modem's WLFW service: walleye-wifi-wcn3990 cannot be proven before the modem runs (walleye-modem-mss-proof)
question: What must run before ath10k snoc can scan on the Pixel 2, and does walleye-wifi-wcn3990's blocked_by list say so?

brief: The lost tail is one block of the ABL's code, not a length cut; header root= refuted; cause not known yet; ranked candidates with a RAM-only try
question: What cuts the bootloader's command line after androidboot.pk=g-pxl-p, losing slot_suffix, want_initramfs, rootwait, ro, init=/init and force_normal_boot?
found: COUNTED from captured text: Android b's line (android-b-cmdline-and-boot-props.txt) puts, after androidboot.pk=g-pxl-p, exactly six words in a fixed order: slot_suffix=_b want_initramfs rootwait ro init=/init androidboot.force_normal_boot=1. Run 8 (header ~377 chars, line 1364) and run 9 (header 149, line ~1136) lose all six, at the same word, though the totals differ by ~228 = the header difference: so it is NOT a buffer or length limit (a limit would cut at the same total, not the same word); everything BEFORE pk (verifiedbootstate=orange, keymaster, root=PARTUUID, bootdevice, serialno, boottime, baseband, panel, ..., pk) is present and equal. FROM SOURCE (CAF ABL UpdateCmdLine.c, generic, not the Pixel's closed build): the slot suffix, the initramfs word (skip_initramfs there; want_initramfs on the Pixel), ' rootwait ro init=/init' and the root path are appended in ONE conditional block after all other words, guarded by multi-slot boot and by NOT finding 'root=' in the header command line; so a block skipped whole gives exactly the symptom (all words after the last unconditional one, gone together). The Pixel's build differs (it puts root=PARTUUID early and force_normal_boot last), so the generic guard is a pointer to the SHAPE, not the proof. REFUTED by reading: (a) 'header contains root=': device.toml:103 header is 'clk_ignore_unused ignore_loglevel panic=5 androidboot.hardware=walleye androidboot.console=ttyMSM0 androidboot.dtbo_idx=3', no root=; the ABL's own root=PARTUUID is in the line (run 10); (b) a size limit (above); (c) a kernel-side cut (arm64 COMMAND_LINE_SIZE 2048, /proc/cmdline 1136). Not read: the Pixel ABL itself (closed), libavb: avb_slot_verify's own appended words (androidboot.vbmeta.*) are absent from Android b's line too (DT vbmeta node instead), so AVB state does not explain the difference by itself. RANKED CANDIDATES for what makes the Pixel's block be skipped: 1. the boot slot's state: Android b is the slot marked successful, ours is slot a just switched to with retry 1 and successful no (runs 8, 9; the slot suffix, initramfs and force_normal_boot words may be added only for a slot the ABL treats as normal); 2. the image: header v0 fields (ramdisk present, dtb appended, os_version, a footer 'algorithm NONE' by avbtool 1.4) vs Android b's boot image; 3. the boot path (a normal boot of a flashed slot, which is all we have tried). SMALLEST CHECKS, no phone change beyond what the procedure already does: (A) READ ONLY: run 10 and run 12 captured the line for slot a after it was marked successful? run 12 ended with ssh on the new slot: read its /proc/cmdline from run12/stdout.txt (keeper's build dir): if the tail is present once the slot is marked successful or the retry count is up, candidate 1 stands; (B) RAM ONLY: fastboot boot of the same production image with Android b's own 299-char header words and no change to flags: tests the header (candidate 2) without flashing; (C) the stock boot_a image booted from slot a with flags as in run 9 (the way back already does the slot switch): a full line there kills candidate 2. Whether image-avb-footer-in-rust is the fix is NOT known yet: no read shows the ABL checks the footer for this block; it is worth building only if (B)/(C) point at the image. Step 21 already accepts the slot from root=PARTUUID, so this item blocks nothing.

brief: The cut is not length, header or footer; it travels with flashed normal boot on slot a (every cut line is slot a, every whole line slot b); three RAM-or-flash checks tell the candidates apart

found: Cause not proven; the bootloader is closed and not read. Counted from captured lines (cmdline-cut-cause-evidence.md): cut lines are 1122 and 1136 characters while whole lines reach 1393 and 1401, so not total length; headers of 135, 149 and 373 characters all cut at the same word, and the bootloader's own words up to pk are 986 characters each time, so not our header; fastboot-boot images carrying the same AVB footer (algorithm NONE, avbtool 1.4) get the whole tail, so not the footer alone. What is left travels together in every capture: flashed normal boot, and slot a (all cut lines slot a, all whole lines slot b; no line with slot_suffix=_a was ever read from any image). Ranked candidates: (1) the normal-boot path on slot a drops the slot words for any image; (2) something in our image (header os version 15 / patch 2026-11 against stock 11 / 2025-11, kernel or ramdisk size, DTB) on the normal path; (3) the AVB-footer-as-fix idea (image-avb-footer-in-rust) is the weakest: the footer is the same on the whole-tail RAM boots.
